what_it_does: Command-line flow: read() loads the requested chromosomes of the genome FASTA; main() then tiles every chromosome with overlapping windows at two scales (small = 2,000 bp windows looking for repeat units of 2-1,000 bp; large = 10,000 bp windows looking for units of 1,000-5,000 bp). For every window it asks how often a 10-letter word (k-mer) recurs at each distance (lag), compares that with the same window after its bases were shuffled (hist + smooth on both, excess = real minus shuffled), and reports the best lag, the strength of the signal (max excess), the signal at twice that lag and the share of k-mers that recur at all. No threshold is applied; windows with more than 50 % N get NA. One TSV is written (chrom, scale, start, end, n_frac, max_excess, best_lag, excess_at_2x, recur_frac) and a progress line is printed per chromosome.
inputs: positional: genome FASTA, tag, out TSV, chromosome list (comma list or all); options --small 2000 --large 10000 --small-lag 1000 --large-lag 5000
outputs: one scan TSV (the scan57 table read by 58_scan_calibrate.py); stdout: <tag> <chrom> done
rule_or_threshold: window W = 2000 (small, lags 2..1000) or 10000 (large, lags 1000..5000); upper lag capped at W/2; step = W/2; extra right-aligned last window when the grid leaves a tail; N fraction > 0.5 -> NA row; shuffle permutes only non-N positions (numpy seed 57); excess at lags < max(2, lo) set to -1; best_lag = argmax excess; excess_at_2x = excess[2*best_lag] (nan if beyond range); recur_frac = recurrences within [lo, hi] / valid k-mer positions

what_it_does: Reads a FASTA file as raw bytes and returns a dictionary chromosome name -> sequence (bytes) for the chromosomes asked for, or all of them when no list is given. The name is the first word after the > sign.
inputs: fa = genome FASTA path; want = set of chromosome names or None

what_it_does: Turns a window (already coded as integers A=0 C=1 G=2 T=3, anything else 4) into one integer code per position for the 10-letter word (k-mer) starting there, plus a flag telling whether that word contains a non-ACGT base. Returns (None, None) when the window holds fewer than two k-mers.
inputs: c = integer-coded window (numpy array)
outputs: tuple (k-mer codes array, bad-flag array) or (None, None)
rule_or_threshold: K = 10 (fixed, forward strand only); a k-mer is bad when any of its 10 bases is not A/C/G/T; fewer than 2 k-mers -> None

what_it_does: For one window, finds for every valid 10-mer the distance to the next place the same 10-mer appears (its next recurrence), and counts how many recurrences fall at each distance from 0 to hi. Returns that distance histogram, the number of valid k-mer positions and the number of recurrences whose distance lies within the lag range [lo, hi].
inputs: c = integer-coded window; lo, hi = lag range in bp
outputs: tuple (histogram array of length hi+1, n valid k-mer positions, n recurrences within [lo, hi]); degenerate windows give (zeros, 1, 0)
rule_or_threshold: k-mers containing non-ACGT bases are ignored; distances > hi are dropped from the histogram; rec counts lo <= distance <= hi

what_it_does: Smooths a lag histogram by replacing the count at each lag by the sum of counts in a band of plus or minus 6 % of that lag (at least plus or minus 1 bp), then divides by the number of k-mer positions so that windows of different content are comparable.
inputs: h = histogram array; nv = number of valid k-mer positions; rel = band width (default 0.06)
outputs: smoothed, normalised array of the same length
rule_or_threshold: band half-width w = max(1, round(0.06 * lag)); value = sum of h[lag-w .. lag+w] / max(1, nv)

what_it_does: Parses the command line, loads the chromosomes, and for every chromosome, scale and window computes the N fraction, shuffles the non-N bases of the window (seed 57), builds the smoothed recurrence histogram of the real and of the shuffled window, takes their difference (excess), and writes the lag with the largest excess, that excess, the excess at twice the lag and the recurrence fraction. Windows that are more than half N are written with NA values.
inputs: command line (see __script__); genome FASTA
rule_or_threshold: as in __script__: W 2000/10000, lags 2..1000 / 1000..5000 capped at W/2, step W/2, right-aligned tail window, N > 0.5 -> NA, excess[<max(2,lo)] = -1, seed 57

what_it_does: Command-line flow: intervals() loads the masks (EDTA TE annotation, the two TRF beds of known tandem repeats with unit >= 7 bp, the step-02 satellite arrays) and two optional validation sets (56 validated HMM runs, step-36 intervals). main() reads every scan57_<tag>_job*.tsv window row (NA rows skipped), splits them by scale, defines the null as ordinary windows (no N, no overlap with TRF or step-02 arrays; TEs and SSRs stay in) and takes the p95 / p99 / p99.9 quantiles of their max excess (two codings, see rule). For each tier, regions_of_scale() chains consecutive windows above the tier with compatible lags into candidate regions, union_regions() merges small- and large-scale regions that overlap with compatible units, the candidates are written as a BED, and the validation table reports total Mb, recall of the validated runs and of step-36 intervals, the share of step-02 bp recovered and the new Mb outside step-02 arrays by unit class (TE_derived when EDTA covers more than half of the outside part).
inputs: positional: tag, scan57 dir (scan57_<tag>_job*.tsv), func genome folder, pipeline out (fClaHyb_<tag>_satellites/02_satellite_arrays.tsv, 36_characterized_intervals.bed), hmm56 dir (56_runs_validated_q0.9.bed, optional), dest; option --null lag7|coded0; annotation files via satpaths.func_path: fClaHyb_<tag>.TEanno.sorted.gff3.gz, TRF/fClaHyb_<tag>.TRF.mini_7-60bp.bed.gz, TRF/fClaHyb_<tag>.TRF.sat_gt60bp.bed.gz
rule_or_threshold: MIN_LAG = 7; tiers 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.999; null window = n_frac == 0 and 0 bp overlap with TRF (unit >= 7) and step-02 arrays; null coding lag7 (default) = quantiles over null windows with best lag >= 7; coded0 = windows with lag < 7 counted as excess 0; tandem window = max_excess > tier and lag >= 7; unit classes 2-6 / 7-39 / 40-60 / 61-1000 / >1000 bp; TE_derived when TE bp > 0.5 x bp outside step-02

what_it_does: Takes a list of (start, end) intervals, sorts them and merges every interval that overlaps or touches the previous one, so that each base is covered once.
inputs: v = list of (start, end) tuples
outputs: sorted list of merged [start, end] pairs
rule_or_threshold: merge when start <= end of the current merged interval

what_it_does: Reads one or more interval files (BED, GFF or a step-02 array table), collects the intervals of each chromosome and merges them (merge_sorted), returning per chromosome two sorted arrays of starts and ends. A missing file stops the run unless required=False, in which case it is skipped with a warning (used only for the validation sets).
inputs: paths = list of file paths (plain or .gz); kind = gff | tsv02 | bed; required flag
rule_or_threshold: gff: records of type repeat_region, target_site_duplication, long_terminal_repeat are skipped, start converted from 1-based to 0-based; tsv02: columns chrom / start_0based / end (header row skipped); bed: columns 1-3; lines starting with # or track skipped

what_it_does: Counts how many base pairs of the stretch [s, e) on chromosome c are covered by the merged intervals of that chromosome; 0 when the chromosome has none.
inputs: iv = intervals dict from intervals(); c, s, e

what_it_does: Returns the pieces of the stretch [s, e) on chromosome c that are NOT covered by the merged intervals, i.e. the part of a candidate that lies outside the known arrays.
inputs: iv = intervals dict; c, s, e

what_it_does: Decides whether two repeat-unit lengths (lags) describe the same repeat: they must be equal or one must be 2x or 3x the other, within 10 % of that multiple. A zero lag is never compatible.
inputs: a, b = two lags in bp
rule_or_threshold: r = larger / smaller; k = round(r); compatible when k <= 3 and |r - k| <= 0.1 * k; a == 0 or b == 0 -> False

what_it_does: Walks the windows of one scale in genome order, keeps only tandem windows (excess above the tier and lag >= 7 bp), and chains consecutive windows on the same chromosome that overlap or touch and whose lag is compatible with the lag of the window added last; each chain becomes one candidate region (_close).
inputs: R = list of window rows (chrom, start, end, n_frac, max_excess, best_lag) of one scale; thr = tier quantile; sc = scale name
outputs: list of regions [chrom, start, end, max excess, unit lag, median lag, n windows, scale]
rule_or_threshold: keep window when max_excess > thr and best_lag >= MIN_LAG (7); extend region when same chrom, window start <= region end and compatible(lag, last lag)

what_it_does: Finishes one chain of windows: records the chromosome and span, the largest excess, the unit = lag of the window with the largest excess (CB05), the median lag of all member windows, the number of windows and the scale.
inputs: cur = [chrom, start, end, list of excesses, list of lags]; sc = scale
outputs: region list [chrom, s, e, max_ex, unit, median lag, n windows, scale]
rule_or_threshold: unit = lag at argmax(excess); median lag written alongside

what_it_does: Merges candidate regions of any scale that overlap on the same chromosome when their units are compatible: the merged region takes the wider span, the sum of windows, the excess / unit / median of the member with the larger excess, and scale small+large if both scales contributed. Overlapping regions with incompatible units are left separate and counted.
inputs: regs = list of regions from regions_of_scale()
outputs: tuple (merged region list, number of overlapping pairs left unmerged)
rule_or_threshold: overlap test: next start < current end; compatible() on the unit lags

what_it_does: Runs the whole calibration: loads masks and validation sets, reads the scan windows, computes the null quantiles per scale and writes them, then for each tier builds and merges the candidate regions, writes the candidate BED, and computes per tier: region Mb (sum and union), candidate counts, recall of the validated HMM runs and of the step-36 intervals, share of step-02 bp covered, new Mb outside step-02 by unit class and the TE_derived class. Prints the quantile table and one summary line per tier.
inputs: command line + files listed under __script__
outputs: 58_null_quantiles.tsv (scale, n_windows, n_clean_null, n_clean_null_lag7, p95/p99/p99.9 coded0 and lag7, null_used), 58_candidates_p<tier>.bed, 58_validation.tsv (17 columns), stdout
rule_or_threshold: as in __script__; recall = bp of the validation set covered by candidates / its total bp (NA when the file is absent)

what_it_does: Command-line flow: imports the helpers of val58_new (step-02 arrays, TRF calls, genome fetch, candidate classes) and the merged-interval helpers of 58_scan_calibrate. main() takes every tier candidate of 58 that lies at least partly outside the step-02 arrays with lag >= 7 bp, cuts the first 20 kb (and 10 / 40 kb for the sweep) of its sequence, shuffles it in dinucleotide blocks, and measures two signals above the shuffle: the recurrence excess at the candidate lag (k-mers that come back one unit later) and the 3-copy chain excess (k-mers that come back one AND two units later). tier_of() turns the two excesses into new_array / new_pair / weak. TRF support (fraction covered by compatible TRF calls) and the share covered by merged EDTA TE intervals are added. Writes a coloured BED, the per-candidate statistics table, a threshold sweep and a stdout summary (n, Mb, TRF shares per class and tier; total new-array Mb and non-TE Mb).
inputs: positional: tag, cal58 dir (58_candidates_p<tier>.bed), func genome folder (fClaHyb_<tag>.TEanno.sorted.gff3.gz via satpaths; TRF/fClaHyb_<tag>.TRF.bed.gz), pipeline out (02_satellite_arrays.tsv), genome FASTA + .fai; options --tier 0.999 --test-kb 20 --chain-cut 0.01 --rec-cut 0.02 --trf-cover 0.5 --no-sweep
outputs: <cal58>/58b_new_candidates.bed (BED9, name tier|unit<lag>|class|TE<share>|TRF<0/1>|TRFcov<fraction>, colour by tier), <cal58>/58b_new_candidates.tsv (16 columns, input of 58c), <cal58>/58b_tier_sweep.tsv, stdout summary
rule_or_threshold: test length 20 kb (first 20,000 bp of the candidate); rec excess = rec_at(real) - rec_at(shuffled); chain excess = chain_at(real) - chain_at(shuffled); new_array if chain excess > 0.01, else new_pair if rec excess > 0.02, else weak; TRF support = cover >= 0.5; TE if merged EDTA overlap > 0.5 of the candidate; sweep over chain cut and rec cut in {0.005, 0.01, 0.02} and test length in {10, 20, 40} kb; numpy seed 58

what_it_does: Assigns the tier of one candidate from its two excess values: new_array when the 3-copy chain excess is above the chain cut (at least three tandem copies), otherwise new_pair when the recurrence excess is above the recurrence cut (a unit that recurs once but does not chain), otherwise weak.
inputs: ch = chain excess; r = recurrence excess; chain_cut; rec_cut
rule_or_threshold: ch > chain_cut (default 0.01) -> new_array; else r > rec_cut (default 0.02) -> new_pair; else weak

what_it_does: Loads masks and candidate lists, then for every candidate computes the recurrence and chain excesses at each test length, assigns the tier at the chosen test length, computes TRF support (as-is flag and coverage fraction), the TE share from merged EDTA intervals, writes the BED and TSV rows, fills the sweep counters and prints the summaries.
inputs: as in __script__
outputs: 58b_new_candidates.bed, 58b_new_candidates.tsv (chrom, start_0based, end, tier, lag, unit_class, out_of_02_bp, te_share_merged, trf_asis, trf_cover, trf_support, rec_excess, chain_excess, n_chained_positions, n_kmer_positions, test_bp), 58b_tier_sweep.tsv (test_kb, chain_cut, rec_cut, unit_class, tier, n, Mb_outside_02, trf_cover_supported_share), stdout
rule_or_threshold: as in __script__; BED colours new_array 31,119,180 / new_pair 235,104,52 / weak 180,178,169

what_it_does: Module of helpers (imported by 58b and 58c) plus a stand-alone report. Run from the command line it loads the step-02 arrays, the full TRF call list, a genome fetcher and the tier candidates outside step-02 by unit class; for every unit class it computes TRF support for every candidate (as-written flag and coverage fraction), then on a random sample of candidates per class tests the first 20 kb of sequence against a dinucleotide-block shuffle (recurrence excess at the lag, 3-copy chain excess) and prints one line per class: n, Mb, share with TRF as-coded, share with TRF cover >= cut, median cover, share supported by recurrence, by chain, and by chain plus TRF cover. Nothing is written to disk.
inputs: positional: tag, cal58 dir (58_candidates_p<tier>.bed), tier, func genome folder (TRF/fClaHyb_<tag>.TRF.bed.gz via satpaths), pipeline out (fClaHyb_<tag>_satellites/02_satellite_arrays.tsv), genome FASTA + .fai, optional n (sample size, default 200); options --trf-cover 0.5 --min-per 7
rule_or_threshold: sample n = 200 per class (random seed 58; numpy seed 58 for the shuffle); test length 20,000 bp; supported if rec excess > 0.02; chain supported if chain excess > 0.01; TRF cover cut 0.5; min TRF period 7 bp

what_it_does: Puts a repeat-unit length (lag) into one of four size classes used throughout 58/58b/58c.
inputs: lag in bp

what_it_does: Reads the step-02 satellite array table of one subgenome and returns, per chromosome, the sorted list of (start, end) of the known arrays.
inputs: <out>/fClaHyb_<tag>_satellites/02_satellite_arrays.tsv (columns chrom, start_0based, end)

what_it_does: Counts the base pairs of [s, e) covered by the intervals of chromosome c, summing every overlapping interval separately (a base covered twice counts twice; not a union).
inputs: d = per-chromosome interval dict; c, s, e
rule_or_threshold: scan starts at the first interval with start >= s - 3,000,000 (assumes no interval longer than 3 Mb)

what_it_does: Reads the full Tandem Repeats Finder BED of one subgenome and returns, per chromosome, the sorted TRF calls as (start, end, period, copies); the period and copy number are parsed from the name field (NNbpxC or MOTIFxC).
inputs: TRF/fClaHyb_<tag>.TRF.bed.gz found with satpaths.func_path(func, tag, _TR, ...)
outputs: dict {chrom: sorted list of (start, end, period bp, copies)}
rule_or_threshold: period = the number before bp, or the motif length; names that do not match the pattern are skipped

what_it_does: Decides whether a TRF period and a candidate lag describe the same repeat unit: equal, or one is 2x or 3x the other, within 10 % of that multiple.
inputs: per = TRF period; lag = candidate lag
rule_or_threshold: r = larger / smaller; k = round(r); True when k <= 3 and |r - k| <= 0.1 * k

what_it_does: Looks up the TRF calls that overlap the candidate [s, e), have at least 3 copies and a compatible period. Returns two things: trf_asis = whether any such call exists (the old flag, any period, >= 1 bp overlap) and cover = the fraction of the candidate covered by the union of such calls whose period is at least min_per.
inputs: trf dict from load_trf(); c, s, e; lag; min_per (default 7)
rule_or_threshold: call counts when start < e, end > s, copies >= 3 and compatible_period(period, lag); cover uses only calls with period >= 7; scan starts at start >= s - 200,000; cover = union bp / (e - s)

what_it_does: Opens the genome FASTA with its .fai index and returns a function fetch(c, s, e) that reads the bases of [s, e) on chromosome c directly from disk (no whole-genome load), stripping line breaks.
inputs: fa = genome FASTA path; <fa>.fai (name, length, offset, bases per line, bytes per line)
outputs: fetch function returning bytes of the slice
rule_or_threshold: reads (e - s) x bytes-per-line / bases-per-line + 2 lines, removes newlines, cuts to e - s bytes

what_it_does: Encodes every k-letter word of an integer-coded sequence as one integer, drops words containing a non-ACGT base, and returns the codes and positions sorted by code then position so that successive occurrences of the same word sit next to each other.
inputs: c = integer-coded sequence; k
outputs: tuple (sorted codes, matching positions, n valid positions)
rule_or_threshold: non-ACGT k-mers excluded

what_it_does: Measures the fraction of k-mer positions whose word next appears about one unit (L) further along: a direct count of how much of the sequence is tandemly repeated with that unit.
inputs: c = integer-coded sequence; L = lag; k (10); tol (0.06)
rule_or_threshold: k = 10; next-occurrence distance d counts when (1 - 0.06) L <= d <= (1 + 0.06) L; divided by valid k-mer positions

what_it_does: Measures the fraction of k-mer positions whose word reappears about one unit later AND again about one unit after that (two consecutive ~L steps), i.e. evidence of at least three tandem copies. With count=True also returns the absolute number of chained positions and of k-mer positions.
inputs: c = integer-coded sequence; L = lag; k (10); tol (0.06); count flag
outputs: fraction, or (fraction, n chained positions, n k-mer positions)
rule_or_threshold: both consecutive next-occurrence steps within +/- 6 % of L; 0 when fewer than 2 k-mers

what_it_does: Builds the null sequence for the recurrence tests: cuts the sequence into non-overlapping 2-base blocks, permutes the blocks at random and re-attaches a trailing odd base, so dinucleotide content is kept but any tandem order is destroyed.
inputs: c = integer-coded sequence; nr = numpy random generator
outputs: shuffled integer-coded sequence of the same length
rule_or_threshold: block size 2; odd last base kept at the end

what_it_does: Reads the 58 candidate BED of one tier, computes for each candidate the bp that lie outside the step-02 arrays, keeps candidates with some outside bp and a lag of at least 7 bp, and groups them by unit class.
inputs: <cal>/58_candidates_p<tier>.bed (name scale|lag<unit>|...); a02 dict from load_a02()
outputs: dict {unit class: list of (chrom, s, e, lag, out_bp)}
rule_or_threshold: out_bp = (e - s) - ov(a02, ...); keep when out_bp > 0 and lag >= 7

what_it_does: Command-line flow: parse_bed() reads the 58b candidate BED; main() decides per candidate whether it has TRF support (coverage fraction >= cut, or the as-written flag for old beds), applies keep_rule() to keep new_array candidates and, on the default route, short-unit candidates (7-39 bp) backed by TRF; the kept intervals are numbered <tag>_NEW00001... along the genome and written in the column layout of the step-02 array table so that 03_monomer_copies.py can decompose them. Overlapping kept intervals are counted and reported, not merged.
inputs: positional: tag, 58b bed (58b_new_candidates.bed), out TSV; options --route chain|chain_or_trf (default chain_or_trf) --trf-field cover|asis (default cover) --trf-cover 0.5 --tier 0.999
outputs: the 02-format table new_candidates_02format_<tag>.tsv (array_id, chrom, start_0based, end, array_length_bp, period_mode_bp = 58 unit lag, candidate_tier, unit_class, TE_fraction, TRF_support, source = scan57_p99.9, kept_by, trf_cover); stdout summary
rule_or_threshold: route chain: keep tier new_array only; route chain_or_trf: keep new_array OR (unit_class 7-39 AND TRF support); TRF support = TRFcov >= 0.5 (field cover) or the 58b TRF flag (field asis); the script stops when --trf-field cover is asked but the bed has no TRFcov field

what_it_does: Reads the 58b BED and unpacks its name field (tier|unit<lag>|class|TE<share>|TRF<flag>|TRFcov<fraction>) into one row per candidate with chromosome, start, end, tier, lag, unit class, TE share, TRF flag and TRF coverage (None for beds written before the TRFcov field existed).
inputs: path of 58b_new_candidates.bed
outputs: list of tuples (chrom, s, e, tier, lag, cls, te, trf_flag, trf_cover or None)

what_it_does: Decides whether one candidate enters the array table and why: a new_array candidate is always kept (kept_by new_array); on the chain_or_trf route a candidate with a 7-39 bp unit and TRF support is kept as <tier>+TRF; everything else is dropped.
inputs: tier, cls = unit class, trf = TRF support flag, route
outputs: kept_by label (new_array, new_pair+TRF, weak+TRF) or None
rule_or_threshold: tier == new_array -> keep; route == chain_or_trf and cls == 7-39 and trf -> keep; else None

what_it_does: Parses the options, reads the bed, checks that the TRFcov field exists when it is needed, applies the support and keep rules to the candidates in genome order, numbers the kept ones, counts kept intervals that overlap the previous one, writes the 02-format table and prints counts and Mb per kept_by label.
inputs: as in __script__
rule_or_threshold: array_id = <tag>_NEW<5-digit running number>; array_length_bp = end - start; source = scan57_p<tier x 100>

what_it_does: Command-line flow (iterative multi-consensus decomposition of every candidate array into monomer copies): main() reads the array table (step-02 or 58c format), marks arrays below --min-array-bp as skipped, checks the checkpoint fingerprint (restart from scratch when the inputs or the script changed, otherwise resume), then runs decompose_array() per array (in-process or in a process pool initialised by _worker_init). decompose_array() takes the array sequence from the genome (faidx_lite), calls _decompose_at() for the seed period (and per/2, 2*per with --seed-multiples), which picks a seed copy, runs StringDecomposer against a growing library of class consensuses (run_sd + ordered_valid_calls), clusters the copies into monomer classes (cluster_copies / same_class / circ_match), rebuilds a consensus per class (consensus_of) and repeats until the copy boundaries stop moving; the best seed by mean identity is kept. Per array it writes the class consensuses, one row per monomer copy (strand, phase, identity, completeness, QC flags, sequence) and an iteration trace; at the end a status row for every input array.
inputs: options --genome FASTA --arrays table (array_id, chrom, start_0based, end, period_mode_bp, array_length_bp) --tag --out --threads 1 --min-array-bp 5000 --seed-multiples; env RUN_ID; external program stringdecomposer; faidx_lite.py
outputs: <out>/03_monomer_copies.tsv (40 columns), 03_array_consensus.tsv, 03_decomposition_iterations.tsv, 03_array_status.tsv, .03_done_arrays.txt (checkpoint); stale 03_*/04_* outputs renamed *.stale; stdout progress
rule_or_threshold: CLASS_ID 90 % identity, CLASS_COV 0.85, LEN_TOL 0.15, MIN_CLASS 8 copies, MAX_CLASSES 12, ORIENT_MARGIN 3.0, PALIN_ID 80, MAX_ITER 5, BOUNDARY_EPS 2.0 bp, STABLE_ROUNDS 2, MAX_BOOT_BP 150,000, CLUSTER_SAMPLE 600, OVL_FRAC 0.5, BOUND_EPS 0.01, MIN_SEED_PER 7; min array 5,000 bp; LIB_EPS 0.98 is defined but not used

what_it_does: Reverse-complements a DNA string; IUPAC ambiguity letters are complemented too (R<->Y, K<->M, B<->V, D<->H; S, W, N unchanged).
inputs: sequence string

what_it_does: Fraction of G and C letters over the whole sequence length (N and other letters stay in the denominator).
inputs: sequence string

what_it_does: Cleans the list of copy tiles that StringDecomposer reports for one array. StringDecomposer works in 5-kb batches and reports the copies in the batch-overlap zones twice or as partly overlapping tiles. The tiles are sorted by position and checked against the array length (an invalid tile stops the run); then exact duplicates are dropped keeping the higher-identity one, a large overlap keeps the higher-identity tile and drops the other, and a small overlap trims the start of the later tile to the end of the previous one. Counts of the three actions and the trimmed tiles are returned in stats.
inputs: calls = StringDecomposer rows (seq name, monomer label, start, end inclusive, identity, ...); array_length; optional stats dict
outputs: cleaned list of tiles in genomic order; stats gets dup_dropped, overlap_dropped, overlap_trimmed and trimmed = set of (start, end)
rule_or_threshold: ValueError when start < 0, end < start or end >= array_length; exact duplicate (same start and end) -> keep higher identity; overlap > OVL_FRAC (0.5) x shorter tile length -> keep higher identity (a winning later tile is re-checked against the tile before); smaller overlap -> later start = previous end + 1; identity of a trimmed tile is not recomputed

what_it_does: Measures how much the copy boundaries moved between two decomposition rounds: for each copy start of the current round, the distance to the nearest copy start of the previous round, averaged over all current starts. None when either list is empty.
inputs: previous, current = lists of copy start positions
outputs: mean distance in bp (float) or None

what_it_does: Generator that yields (name, uppercase sequence) for every record of a FASTA file. Not called anywhere in this script (the genome is read through faidx_lite.Fai instead); kept as a legacy helper.
inputs: FASTA path

what_it_does: Runs the external program StringDecomposer on the array sequence with the current monomer library and returns the rows of its final_decomposition.tsv (one tile per copy: sequence name, monomer label with a trailing apostrophe for the reverse strand, start, end, identity, second-best label and identity, reliability flag). The step stops if the program fails.
inputs: seq_fa = array FASTA; mono_fa = library FASTA; outdir; second_best flag
outputs: list of tab-split rows of final_decomposition.tsv
rule_or_threshold: command stringdecomposer <seq> <lib> -o <outdir> -t 1 [--second-best]; check=True

what_it_does: Compares copy a with copy b regardless of where the copy starts in the repeat unit (rotation) and of strand: a is aligned as a substring against b doubled (b+b) and against the reverse complement doubled; returns the best identity, the coverage of the shorter over the longer, and the strand that gave it.
inputs: a, b = sequence strings
rule_or_threshold: edlib infix alignment (mode HW); identity = 100 x (1 - edit distance / len(a)); coverage = min(1, len(a) / len(b))

what_it_does: Decides whether two monomer copies belong to the same monomer class: their lengths must differ by at most 15 % of the longer, and the rotation/strand-free identity must reach 90 % with coverage of at least 0.85.
inputs: a, b = copy sequences
rule_or_threshold: |len(a) - len(b)| <= LEN_TOL (0.15) x max length; circ_match identity >= CLASS_ID (90) and coverage >= CLASS_COV (0.85)

what_it_does: Groups the sampled copies of one array into monomer classes by a greedy pass: copies are taken longest first, each is compared with the representative of every existing class and joins the first class that matches (same_class); otherwise it founds a new class, unless 12 classes already exist, in which case it is attached to the representative with the smallest global edit distance. Classes are returned largest first.
inputs: copies = list of copy sequences
outputs: list of member-index lists, sorted by class size descending
rule_or_threshold: MAX_CLASSES 12; overflow assignment by edlib global (NW) edit distance

what_it_does: Builds the consensus sequence of one monomer class: every member copy is globally aligned to a reference copy (the middle member) and, for every reference position, the aligned member bases vote; the most frequent base wins, N never votes, and if the winner is a gap or nobody voted the reference base is kept. The consensus therefore has the length of the reference.
inputs: members = list of copy sequences; ref = reference copy
rule_or_threshold: edlib NW alignment; positions where the reference has a gap (member insertions) are skipped

what_it_does: Set-up run once per worker process: opens the genome through faidx_lite.Fai (random access without loading the genome) and stores the tag, run id and the seed-multiples switch in the module-level dictionary _W used by the other worker functions.
inputs: genome FASTA path, tag, run_id, seed_multiples flag

what_it_does: Returns the full sequence of chromosome c, reading it from the genome only when the chromosome differs from the one cached in _W (one chromosome kept in memory at a time).
inputs: c = chromosome name

what_it_does: Decomposes one array at one seed period. Seed: in the first 150 kb, slides a window in steps of a quarter period over the first 60 kb of starts, skips windows containing N, and takes the window whose bases agree best with the next window one period away as the first library entry C01 (none -> SKIPPED_N_MASKED_NO_CLEAN_SEED). Loop (up to 5 rounds): write the library, run StringDecomposer on the whole array, clean the tiles (ordered_valid_calls), extract the copies (reverse-complemented when on the minus strand), compute the unresolved fraction and the mean boundary shift against the previous round, declare convergence after two consecutive rounds with shift below 2 bp; otherwise keep the good copies, sample up to 600 of them, cluster them into classes, build one consensus per class with at least 8 members as the new library, record the similarity between old and new library, and iterate. Final pass with the fixed library; returns library, cleaned tiles, trace rows, convergence flags and mean identity.
inputs: aid; full = array sequence; boot = first 150 kb; per = seed period; fa = array FASTA path; tmp dir; sub = trial index
outputs: dict: status (None ok or SKIPPED_* code), library [(class name, consensus)], iters (trace rows: aid, iteration, n library monomers, n copies, mean identity, mean boundary shift, library similarity, unresolved fraction, converged), dec (final cleaned tiles), it, rebuilt, conv, stats, mean_id, per
rule_or_threshold: seed scan: i from 0 to min(len(boot) - 2 per, 60000) step max(1, per // 4), window [i, i + 2 per) must be N-free, score = share of equal bases between boot[i:i+per] and boot[i+per:i+2per]; MAX_ITER 5; converged when shift < BOUNDARY_EPS 2.0 bp for STABLE_ROUNDS 2 rounds in a row; good copy = identity >= 60 and |length - per| <= 2 x LEN_TOL x per (0.30 per, the 0.70-1.30 x period bound) and N <= 5 %; < MIN_CLASS 8 good copies -> stop with the seed library; CLUSTER_SAMPLE 600 evenly spaced; class needs >= 8 members; library similarity = mean of 1 - editdist(old, new doubled)/len(old) when class counts match, else 0; StringDecomposer run with --second-best

what_it_does: Processes one array row end to end and never raises: validates period and interval, takes the array sequence from the chromosome, skips arrays shorter than three periods, writes the array to a temporary FASTA, runs _decompose_at for the seed period (plus per/2 and 2*per with --seed-multiples) and keeps the trial with the best mean identity. From the result it builds the status extras (library rebuilt, converged, iterations, period-bound flag, seed periods tested, tile clean-up counts), one consensus row per class (length, GC, copies, share, self-vs-reverse-complement identity and palindromy call) and one row per monomer copy with genomic and array-relative coordinates, strand and how confidently it was resolved, phase offset within the unit, identity to its class consensus, second-best identity and class margin, divergence, matches/mismatches/indels, complete or truncated, boundary copy, AT/GC %, sha1 of the oriented sequence, QC flags and the oriented sequence. Any exception becomes status FAILED:<type>:<message>.
inputs: r = one array row (array_id, chrom, start_0based, end, period_mode_bp); _W (genome, tag, run id, seed-multiples)
outputs: dict aid, status (DECOMPOSED, NO_MONOMER_CALLS, INVALID_PERIOD_OR_INTERVAL, SKIPPED_FEWER_THAN_THREE_PERIODS, SKIPPED_N_MASKED_NO_CLEAN_SEED, FAILED:...), iters, cons rows, mono rows (COLUMNS), nlib, extra (STATUS_EXTRA)
rule_or_threshold: boot = first MAX_BOOT_BP 150,000 bp, needs >= 3 x per; extra seed periods per // 2 and 2 x per only when >= MIN_SEED_PER 7 and boot >= 3 x period; best trial = max mean identity; period_bound_hit = low when dominant consensus length / per <= 0.70 + 0.01, high when >= 1.30 - 0.01, else no; palindromic when consensus vs its reverse complement identity >= PALIN_ID 80; orientation margin = |identity(+) - identity(-)| x 100 vs consensus (NW); strand_status = palindromic / resolved (margin >= ORIENT_MARGIN 3.0) / ambiguous; phase = start of best infix placement in the doubled consensus mod consensus length; complete when |copy length - consensus length| <= 0.15 x consensus length else truncated; AT % over ACGT only; qc_flag: WARN_N_bases if N > 5 % else WARN_low_identity if identity < 70; WARN_SD_unreliable (StringDecomposer ? column); WARN_overlap_trimmed; PASS when none; species from tag prefix Gar -> C. gariepinus else C. macrocephalus; tool_version 1.1.2

what_it_does: Command-line driver: reads the array table, excludes arrays below the minimum length (status SKIPPED_BELOW_MIN_ARRAY_BP), sorts by chromosome and start, warns about overlapping input intervals, builds the checkpoint fingerprint (sha256 of this script plus the array coordinates and periods and the seed-multiples switch); a checkpoint with a different fingerprint or a missing output table parks the old outputs as *.stale and restarts, otherwise it resumes (rows of unfinished arrays are trimmed from the tables, previous statuses carried over, FAILED arrays retried). A fresh run also parks the step-04 family outputs. Arrays are decomposed one by one or in a process pool; rows are written per array in input order and the array id appended to the checkpoint unless it FAILED. Finally the status table for every input array is written and totals printed.
inputs: command line (see __script__); 02-format array table; genome FASTA
outputs: 03_monomer_copies.tsv, 03_array_consensus.tsv (13 columns), 03_decomposition_iterations.tsv (9 columns), 03_array_status.tsv (array_id, chrom, start_0based, end, status, run_id + STATUS_EXTRA), .03_done_arrays.txt; *.stale files; stdout
rule_or_threshold: --min-array-bp 5000; --threads <= 1 runs in-process, else ProcessPoolExecutor chunksize 1; progress line every 5 arrays; checkpoint first line #fingerprint=<sha256>

what_it_does: Command-line flow: applies the StringDecomposer tile clean-up rule of 03_monomer_copies.ordered_valid_calls (imported from that script) to an existing 03_monomer_copies.tsv without rerunning StringDecomposer. main() streams the table one array at a time (arrays must be contiguous; if an array id reappears it switches to a two-pass mode indexed by file offsets), dedup_array() rebuilds the tiles from the array-relative coordinates, drops duplicates and large overlaps, trims small overlaps (and the sequence, coordinates, length, sha1, AT/GC and QC flag of the trimmed copy), renumbers the copies and recomputes the boundary flags; every array writes its kept rows and one log line.
inputs: argv: source 03_monomer_copies.tsv, output prefix; 03_monomer_copies.py (ordered_valid_calls, needs edlib importable)
outputs: <prefix>.tsv (same 40 columns) and <prefix>.dedup_log.tsv (array_id, rows_in, rows_out, dup_dropped, overlap_dropped, overlap_trimmed); stdout totals
rule_or_threshold: same rule as ordered_valid_calls: exact duplicate -> keep higher identity; overlap > 0.5 x shorter tile -> keep higher identity; smaller overlap -> trim the later tile start to the previous end

what_it_does: Cleans the copies of one array: converts each row into a tile (row index, class, array_relative_start, array_relative_end - 1 as inclusive end, identity), hands the tiles to ordered_valid_calls, and for every kept tile copies the original row; if the tile start was trimmed it drops the trimmed bases from the oriented sequence (from its start for a + strand copy, from its end for a - strand copy), updates sha1, array-relative and genomic start, observed length, AT/GC % and adds WARN_overlap_trimmed to qc_flag. monomer_index / monomer_id are renumbered and boundary_copy set for the first and last kept copy. Identity, match/mismatch/indel counts and completeness are left as they were.
inputs: aid; rows = field lists of one array in file order; col = column name -> index
outputs: tuple (kept rows, stats dict with dup_dropped / overlap_dropped / overlap_trimmed)
rule_or_threshold: array length for the bound check = max array_relative_end + 1; AT % over ACGT only; sha1 truncated to 16 hex characters; monomer_id = <aid>_M<5-digit index>

what_it_does: Reads the header, then streams the table array by array, calling dedup_array and writing the kept rows and a log line per array; when an array id turns out not to be contiguous it truncates the outputs, records the file offset of every line per array id and re-processes the table array by array in a second pass. Prints the number of arrays, rows in/out and the drop/trim totals.
inputs: argv source table, output prefix

what_it_does: Library module, not run from the command line: provides the Fai class used by 03_monomer_copies.py (and other scripts) to read one chromosome at a time from the genome FASTA instead of loading the whole assembly into memory.
inputs: genome FASTA path

what_it_does: Class giving random access to a FASTA file. On construction (__init__) it scans the file once and records for every record the byte offset where its sequence starts and the byte length of the sequence block (_index). names() lists the record names; get(name) reads that block from disk, removes line breaks and returns the uppercase sequence; length(name) is the length of get(name) (loads the sequence); sizes() returns the length of every record without decoding, as block bytes minus newline characters. No .fai file is written or read; the index lives in memory.
inputs: path = FASTA path (LF or CRLF line ends)
outputs: Fai object: idx {name: (offset, block length)}; get -> sequence string; sizes -> {name: length}
rule_or_threshold: record name = first word after >; sequences uppercased

what_it_does: Script without functions (top-level code, two modes). export: writes the class consensuses of the new arrays (03_array_consensus.tsv of the new-array 03 run) to a FASTA with headers array_id|monomer_class, for a BLAST against the family consensuses of both subgenomes. assign: reads the BLAST tabular output (query, subject, identity, alignment length, ..., query length, subject length), keeps hits with identity >= 80 % covering >= 50 % of the query consensus, scores each hit as identity x coverage plus 1 point when the subject family belongs to the same subgenome, keeps the best hit per class consensus, and writes one row per class with the family it matched (or new:<array_id> when nothing matched); prints counts of same-subgenome, cross-subgenome and new assignments.
inputs: argv: export <G> <new03 dir> <out fa> | assign <G> <new03 dir> <blast tsv> <out tsv>; <new03 dir>/03_array_consensus.tsv (array_id, monomer_class, consensus_sequence); BLAST subject ids formatted <subgenome>|<family>
outputs: export: FASTA; assign: TSV (array_id, monomer_class, family, hit_subgenome, identity, coverage) + stdout counts
rule_or_threshold: hit kept when identity >= 80 and alignment length / query length >= 0.5; score = identity x coverage + (1 if subject subgenome == G else 0), i.e. a same-subgenome hit wins unless the cross-subgenome hit is more than 1 point better; no hit -> family new:<array_id>

what_it_does:
Command-line step that turns the ordered monomer copies (tiles) of every candidate satellite array into a string of symbols (C confident copy, W weak copy, J junk tile, G uncovered stretch), fits a two-state hidden Markov model (state A = inside an array, state B = background) and cuts each array into runs = maximal stretches of tiles that the model judges to be array. Flow: (1) parse arguments; build a Gaps object when --gaps or --scan-n is given; (2) paths() reads 02_satellite_arrays.tsv + 03_monomer_copies.tsv of every --out folder and builds one observation path per (array, gap-free segment); (3) a seeded random sample of --train-n arrays is drawn from the sorted array ids; (4) baum_welch() learns the model on all segments of the sampled arrays and 56_hmm_params.tsv is written; (5) the step-36 runs of the first --out folder (36_characterized_intervals.bed) are read for comparison; (6) for every --post cut-off, fb() gives each tile its posterior P(array); each maximal stretch of tiles with P(array) >= post is trimmed to its first and last confident tile and written as a run to 56_runs_post

.bed when it holds >= --min-c confident copies; (7) nested helpers bp() and inter() compute merged bp of the HMM runs, of the step-36 runs and of their intersection -> 56_summary.tsv; (8) parameters and summary are printed.
inputs: --out folder(s): 02_satellite_arrays.tsv, 03_monomer_copies.tsv; first --out folder: 36_characterized_intervals.bed (optional); --gaps assembly-gap BED; --genome FASTA (only with --scan-n)
outputs:
/56_hmm_params.tsv; /56_runs_post

.bed per posterior cut (BED6; name = array_id|hmm|n_conf|n_tiles|mean_post|g|t); /56_summary.tsv (posterior_cut, n_hmm_runs, hmm_Mb, step36_Mb, shared_Mb, hmm_only_Mb, step36_only_Mb)
rule_or_threshold: defaults: --conf 80, --weak 65, --gap-units 0.5, --post 0.5,0.8,0.95, --min-c 4, --train-n 400; random seed 56; run = maximal stretch with P(array) >= post, trimmed to its first/last confident tile, kept if >= min-c confident tiles; mean_post = mean P(array) over the trimmed stretch; paths with fewer than 2 tiles are skipped

what_it_does: Reads every array and its monomer copies from one or more pipeline folders and converts the copies of each array, in genomic order, into a list of symbols: 0 = C confident copy, 1 = W weak copy, 2 = J junk tile, 3 = G uncovered stretch (one G per stretch). Exact duplicate tiles (same start and end as the previous copy) are skipped. When a Gaps object is given, a copy overlapping an assembly gap is dropped, and a gap or contig join between two consecutive copies ends the current path and starts a new segment (key = (array_id, segment number)). Returns the paths and the merged 02 array table.
inputs: outs: list of pipeline folders each with 02_satellite_arrays.tsv (array_id, chrom, period_mode_bp) and 03_monomer_copies.tsv (array_id, genomic_start_0based, genomic_end, best_alignment_identity, complete_or_truncated, chrom); conf, weak, gapu; gaps = Gaps object or None
outputs: returns (P, arr): P[(array_id, segment)] = (chrom, numpy array of symbols, list of (start, end) per symbol, index of the --out table); arr = merged 02 table; prints table/array/path/duplicate counts and the number of extra gap segments and dropped copies
rule_or_threshold: C = complete AND identity >= conf (80); W = identity >= weak (65) but not C (a truncated copy with identity >= 80 is also W); J = identity < 65; G inserted when the next copy starts more than gap-units x period (0.5 x period_mode_bp, period at least 1 bp) after the end of the previous coverage; unparsable identity = 0; duplicate = same (start, end) as the previous copy; gap test on the copy itself is open (closed=False), on the stretch between two copies closed=True; chrom taken from the 02 table, else from the copy row

what_it_does: Forward-backward algorithm for the two-state model: given one symbol sequence and the model (transition matrix T, emission matrix E, start probabilities pi) it computes for every tile the probability of being in state A (array) versus B (background), taking the whole sequence into account. Returns the scaled forward values, backward values, the scaling factors (their log-sum is the log-likelihood) and the posterior matrix g (one row per tile; column 0 = P(array)).
inputs: obs (integer array of symbols 0-3), T (2x2), E (2x4), pi (2)
outputs: returns (a, b, c, g); g[:,0] is the per-tile posterior P(array) used by main()
rule_or_threshold: standard scaled forward-backward; posterior normalised per tile to sum to 1

what_it_does: Learns the hidden Markov model parameters from the training symbol sequences by expectation-maximisation (Baum-Welch). Starts from hand-set values (stay in the same state 0.98; array emits C .70 W .20 J .08 G .02; background emits C .05 W .15 J .50 G .30; start 0.5/0.5), re-estimates transitions, emissions and start probabilities from the posteriors each iteration, and after each iteration swaps the two states if needed so that state 0 is always the one emitting more confident copies (the array state). Stops when the log-likelihood no longer changes or after the maximum number of iterations.
inputs: seqs: list of symbol arrays (all segments of the training arrays); iters (default 30)
outputs: returns (T, E, pi, log-likelihood, number of iterations run)
rule_or_threshold: sequences shorter than 2 tiles ignored; pseudocount 1e-6 on emission counts; converged when |ll - ll_prev| < 1e-4 x |ll_prev|; max 30 iterations; state order fixed by E[0,C] >= E[1,C]

what_it_does: Command-line driver; the numbered flow is in the __script__ row. Fits the model once per haplotype on the union of all --out tables, then for each posterior cut-off scores every path with fb(), cuts runs, writes the run BED and compares the run set with the step-36 runs. Two nested helpers: bp(iv) returns the total bp of the merged (non-overlapping) intervals per chromosome; inter(x, y) returns the bp shared between two interval sets.
inputs: command-line arguments (see __script__); P and arr from paths(); 36_characterized_intervals.bed of the first --out folder
outputs:
56_hmm_params.tsv (iterations, loglik, P(A->A), P(B->B), train_arrays, train_paths, tables, emission_A, emission_B); 56_runs_post

.bed; 56_summary.tsv; printed params and summary rows
rule_or_threshold: training sample: min(--train-n, n arrays) array ids chosen without replacement with numpy rng seed 56 from the sorted array ids; run kept if >= --min-c (4) confident tiles; run edges = start of first and end of last confident tile in the stretch

what_it_does: Command-line step (everything happens in main()) that checks every copy-chain run against a background null built from a genome-wide tandem-repeat signal track, and keeps only runs whose signal exceeds a background quantile. Flow: (1) parse arguments; exactly one of --signal (step-48 1-kb tandem-signal bedgraph) or --scan57 (step-57 any-lag scan table) must be given; (2) read_runs() loads the runs to test, bed() loads the step-36 runs, read_track() loads the signal bins; (3) candidate intervals = step-02 array intervals (--a02) + step-36 runs + the tested runs + every --exclude BED, merged per chromosome; (4) background = every --subsample-th track bin whose midpoint lies outside all candidate intervals; values sorted; share of exactly-zero bins recorded; stop with an error if no background bin; (5) chromosomes carrying runs but absent from the track stop the script unless --allow-untested (their runs are then kept and flagged untested); (6) per run: score = bp-weighted mean of the track value over the overlapping bins, number of bins, modal best lag, lag_matches_unit, few_bins flag, bp shared with step-36; (7) per quantile q: threshold = background value at quantile q; a run is kept when its score > threshold (or it is untested); kept runs written to 56_runs_validated_q<q>.bed; one benchmark row per q; (8) per-run table val56_runs_<tag>.tsv and benchmark table val56_benchmark_<tag>.tsv written.
inputs: --runs (56 BED or runs TSV), --bed36 (step-36 BED), --a02 (02_satellite_arrays.tsv with chrom, start_0based, end), --signal bedgraph or --scan57 TSV (chrom, start, end, scale, max_excess, best_lag), --exclude BEDs
outputs: <dest>/56_runs_validated_q<q>.bed per q (BED6); <dest>/val56_runs_<tag>.tsv (run_id, chrom, start0, end, bp, score, n_bins, few_bins, untested, modal_lag, unit_bp, lag_matches_unit, shared36_bp, kept_q<q> per q); <dest>/val56_benchmark_<tag>.tsv (tag, track, q, threshold, runs_kept, runs_total, kept_Mb, dropped_Mb, shared_with_36_Mb, frac_36_bp_kept, added_beyond_36_Mb, runs_few_bins, runs_untested, background_bins, background_zero_share, background_rule, subsample, min_bins)
rule_or_threshold: defaults: --q 0.80,0.90,0.95; --min-bins 2; --subsample 1; --scan57-scale both; threshold = sorted background value at index int(q x n_background); kept if score > threshold (strict); untested runs (no track on their chromosome) kept at every q with score 'untested'; few_bins = fewer than --min-bins overlapping bins (flag only, the run is still decided on its weighted mean); lag_matches_unit = yes when the modal lag lies within 6 % of 1x, 2x or 0.5x unit_bp

what_it_does: Reads a BED file into a dictionary chromosome -> sorted list of (start, end, name). The name is column 4 when present (and name=True), otherwise 'chrom:start-end'. Comment, track and blank lines are skipped.
inputs: p = BED path; name flag
outputs: returns {chrom: [(start, end, name)]} sorted per chromosome

what_it_does: Loads the runs to be tested in either of two formats, decided from the header line: a runs/catalogue TSV when it has a run_id column (uses run_id, chrom, start0, end and optional unit_bp), otherwise a 56 BED (name column = run id, no unit). Returns chromosome -> sorted list of (start, end, run id, unit_bp or None).
inputs: p = 56 BED or runs-of-record / catalogue TSV
rule_or_threshold: unit_bp blank or 'NA' -> None

what_it_does: Loads the genome-wide signal bins. With --scan57: the step-57 scan table, keeping rows of the chosen window scale (small/large/both) and skipping N-rich windows written as NA; each bin = (start, end, max_excess, best_lag). With --signal: the step-48 bedgraph (chrom, start, end, value), lag = None. Also returns the longest bin length (used to start the overlap search early enough).
inputs: a = parsed arguments (a.scan57, a.scan57_scale, a.signal)
outputs: returns ({chrom: sorted [(start, end, value, lag)]}, max bin length)
rule_or_threshold: scan57 rows with max_excess or best_lag == NA dropped; scale filter unless --scan57-scale both

what_it_does: Driver; the numbered flow is in the __script__ row. Three nested helpers: inside(c, x) tells whether position x lies within any merged candidate interval (binary search); cov(d, c, s, e) returns the bp of [s, e) overlapped by the intervals of d (used for bp shared with step-36; search starts 5 Mb before s); score(c, s, e) returns the bp-weighted mean track value over bins overlapping the run, the number of overlapping bins and the modal best lag (lag weighted by overlap bp).
inputs: see __script__
outputs: see __script__; prints one line per q and a background line
rule_or_threshold: score weight = overlap bp between bin and run; bins with zero overlap ignored; background bin midpoint = (start + end) // 2; error 'no background bins' stops the script; error on chromosomes without track unless --allow-untested

what_it_does: Library module with no command-line flow: the class Gaps represents assembly gaps as hard stops. A gap is an interval of the assembly-gap BED (detgaps; runs of N placeholders) or a zero-length row (two contigs joined without Ns: the sequence across the join was not observed either); runs of N found directly in the FASTA can be added. Used by 56 (a run ends at a gap), 59e and 61 (no interruption or chain link across a gap) and 61b (windows never touch a gap).
inputs: assembly-gap BED, optional genome FASTA
outputs: Gaps object with between(), gaps_in(), count()

what_it_does: Class holding the assembly gaps and contig joins of a genome per chromosome, with a query between(chrom, a, b) that answers whether a gap or join lies between two positions. Methods: __init__ (load), scan_fasta (find N runs), between (query), gaps_in (list the rows a query would see), count (number of rows).
inputs: bed (gap BED path or None), fasta (path or None), min_n (default 10), include_joins (default True)
outputs: attributes iv = {chrom: sorted unique (start, end)}, starts = {chrom: [start...]}
rule_or_threshold: see the method rows

what_it_does: Loads the gap BED: every row (chrom, start, end) becomes a gap interval; a zero-length row (start == end) is kept as a contig join point when include_joins is True, except a 0-0 row, which marks the chromosome start and is skipped. When a FASTA is given, scan_fasta() adds runs of N. Intervals are de-duplicated and sorted and a list of starts is kept for binary search.
inputs: bed, fasta, min_n, include_joins
rule_or_threshold: zero-length rows skipped when include_joins is False or when start == 0

what_it_does: Reads the genome FASTA sequence by sequence and records every run of at least min_n consecutive N (case-insensitive) as a gap interval, so a catalogue built on a genome without a gap BED still stops at Ns.
inputs: fasta path, min_n (10 by default)
rule_or_threshold: N run length >= min_n (default 10); chromosome name = first word of the header

what_it_does: Answers whether a gap or join separates positions a and b on chromosome c: True when a gap interval overlaps [a, b), or when a zero-length join lies strictly inside (a, b); with closed=True a join exactly at a or b also counts (use closed=True for the stretch between two neighbouring copies or runs, closed=False for a copy itself). Searches backwards from the last gap starting before b.
inputs: c, a, b, closed (default False)
rule_or_threshold: False when b < a, or when b == a and not closed; gap overlap test: gap end > a and gap start < b; join test: a < s < b (open) or a <= s <= b (closed); backward scan stops when a gap ends <= a and starts more than 10,000,000 bp before a

what_it_does: Lists all gap and join rows of chromosome c that the closed between(c, a, b) test would see, for reports.
inputs: c, a, b
rule_or_threshold: join rows with a <= start <= b; gap rows with end > a and start < b

what_it_does: Returns the total number of gap and join rows loaded over all chromosomes.

Builds the validated satellite catalogue of one subgenome (G = Gar or Mac): one row per validated run with copy statistics, family, quality gates, gene-array class, TE overlap, centromere flags and tier. Nearly all work is at module top level. Flow: (1) parse positional arguments G OUT H N03 HN FAMNEW CLUS FUNC FA DEST and options; P = OUT/fClaHyb_<G>_satellites; overlay folder = --overlays or <grandparent of FUNC>/satellite_FISH/annotation_overlays/<G>; (2) read the sequence-cluster table (family -> seq_cluster for subgenome G) and the famnew table ((array_id, monomer_class) -> family for new arrays); (3) read period_mode_bp per array from the existing 02 table and the new-array 02 table; (4) runs() reads the validated runs H/<--validated-name> plus a legacy HN/56_runs_post0.95.bed; runs are split into source 'existing' (array in old 02 table) and 'new'; the script stops if any run array is missing from both 02 tables; (5) load_copies() loads the copies of the needed arrays from both 03_monomer_copies.tsv; arrays split by step 56 at assembly gaps are counted (NSEG) so that their rows get array_id <array>~g<segment>; (6) consensus GC per (array, class) read from 03_array_consensus.tsv; (7) EDTA TE features read from the TEanno GFF (repeat_region / target_site_duplication / long_terminal_repeat records excluded) and merged into a clipped union per chromosome; (8) step-31 centromere candidates read from 31_centromere_summary.tsv; (9) genome FASTA opened through its .fai for gc_of(); (10) stats() computes one row per run; runs with no confident copy go to the dropped list; (11) --carry-new copies the source 'new' rows of an earlier catalogue verbatim (flagged carried_from); (12) overlap resolution on the sorted rows: two overlapping runs of the same family from different sources are merged into one run (stats over the union); otherwise the run with fewer confident copies loses: dropped if contained, else trimmed to the other's edge and recomputed (dropped if nothing remains); overlap_note records what happened; (13) run_id = <G>_E<5 digits> (existing) or <G>_N<5 digits> (new); gates G1/G2/G3 and gates_passed; gate sweep written; (14) 59b classify() called as a module -> element_class and gene_flag per family; 59b tables written; (15) seq_cluster, EDTA_overlap_fraction, putative_centromeric_array_L1 and evidence 'L1' added; (16) cen_candidate_ror: per chromosome the largest cluster of satellite-class runs with unit_class satellite lying <= 100 kb apart; (17) tiers by cumulative share of satellite bp over families ranked by bp; (18) 59_catalogue_<G>.tsv, 59_catalogue_<G>.bed (BED9 coloured by seq_cluster), 59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv, 59_dropped_runs_<G>.tsv and 59_summary_<G>.tsv written and a summary printed. Note: --gaps is accepted by the argument parser but not used anywhere in this script (gap segments come from the 56 BED names).
inputs: P/02_satellite_arrays.tsv, N03/02_satellite_arrays.tsv, H/56_runs_validated_q0.9.bed (or --validated-name), HN/56_runs_post0.95.bed (legacy, optional), P/03_monomer_copies.tsv, N03/03_monomer_copies.tsv, P/03_array_consensus.tsv, N03/03_array_consensus.tsv, FUNC/.../fClaHyb_<G>.TEanno.sorted.gff3.gz (via func_path), P/31_centromere_summary.tsv, genome FASTA FA + FA.fai, FAMNEW tsv (array_id, monomer_class, family), CLUS tsv (subgenome, family, seq_cluster|lineage), --carry-new earlier catalogue, annotation overlays (through 59b)
outputs: DEST/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv (run_id, subgenome, chrom, start0, end, bp, source, array_id, array_id_v46, gap_segment, unit_bp, unit_class, n_conf, n_weak, n_junk, mean_identity_conf, reverse_fraction, run_GC, consensus_GC, G1, G2, G3, gates_passed, dominant_class, family, element_class, gene_flag, seq_cluster, EDTA_overlap_fraction, putative_centromeric_array_L1, cen_candidate_ror, tier, overlap_note, carried_from, evidence); DEST/59_catalogue_<G>.bed (BED9, name = run_id|family|element_class|seq_cluster|<unit>bp|tier, colour by seq_cluster); DEST/59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv (family, bp, share, tier, seq_cluster, element_class); DEST/59b_gene_arrays_<G>.tsv + 59b_gene_arrays_<G>_sweep.tsv; DEST/59_gates_sweep_<G>.tsv; DEST/59_dropped_runs_<G>.tsv (chrom, start0, end, array_id, source, reason); DEST/59_summary_<G>.tsv (kind, value, n_runs, Mb)
rule_or_threshold: confident copy = complete AND identity >= 80; weak = identity 65-80 or truncated with identity >= 80; junk = identity < 65; unit_class: unit <= 6 micro, 7-99 mini, >= 100 satellite; G1 PASS if |run GC - consensus GC of the dominant class| <= 5 points (FAIL when no consensus GC); G2 PASS if mean identity of confident copies >= 85; G3 PASS if reverse-strand fraction of confident copies is NOT between 0.35 and 0.65 (exclusive); gate sweep: G1 3/5/8 points x G2 80/85/90 x G3 bands 0.3-0.7, 0.35-0.65, 0.4-0.6; --gene-cut 0.7 and --unit-cut 0.5 passed to 59b; overlap: same family + different source + neither carried -> merge, else loser = run with n_conf <= the other's; EDTA_overlap_fraction = min(1, union TE bp / run bp); putative_centromeric_array_L1 = yes if the run overlaps a step-31 candidate by > 0 bp (na for non-satellite element classes); cen_candidate_ror cluster gap <= 100,000 bp, largest cluster by summed bp; tiers on satellite-class families ranked by bp: core while cumulative share before the family < 0.5, major < 0.9, minor < 0.99, rare otherwise; non-satellite families tier 'gene_array'; evidence = L1 for every row

what_it_does: Reads the step-03 monomer-copy table and keeps the copies of the requested arrays only. Per copy it stores (start, end, identity, complete?, strand, family_id, monomer_class); copies are sorted along the chromosome and exact duplicate tiles (same start and end as the previous copy) are dropped.
inputs: path = 03_monomer_copies.tsv (columns array_id, genomic_start_0based, genomic_end, best_alignment_identity, complete_or_truncated, strand, family_id, monomer_class); keep = set of array ids
outputs: returns {array_id: [(start, end, identity, complete, strand, family_id, monomer_class)]}; prints copy / array / duplicate counts
rule_or_threshold: unparsable identity = 0; duplicate = same (start, end) as the previous copy of the array

what_it_does: Parses a step-56 run BED into tuples: chromosome, start, end, array id (text before the first '|' in the name) and gap segment number (the 'g<n>' field of the name; 1 when absent).
inputs: bed = 56 BED path (name = array|hmmN|n_conf|n_tiles|mean_post|g<segment>|t<table>)
outputs: returns list of (chrom, start, end, array_id, segment)
rule_or_threshold: segment defaults to 1 when no g<digits> field is present

what_it_does: Returns the number of bp of the interval [s, e) on chromosome c that is covered by the sorted intervals stored in d (used for EDTA TE overlap and step-31 centromere overlap).
inputs: d = {chrom: sorted [(start, end)]}, c, s, e
rule_or_threshold: scan starts at the first interval starting >= s - 2,000,000 bp (an interval longer than 2 Mb starting earlier would be missed)

what_it_does: Reads the sequence of chromosome c from position s to e straight from the genome FASTA using the .fai index (byte offset and line length) and returns its GC content in percent over non-N bases.
inputs: c, s, e; module-level fai index and open FASTA handle (FA, FA.fai)
rule_or_threshold: GC = 100 x (G + C) / max(1, length - N count); uppercase comparison

what_it_does: Computes the catalogue row of one run from the copies of its array that lie inside the run. Confident copies = complete with identity >= 80; without any, the run is returned as None (it is then logged as dropped). From the confident copies it derives the mean identity, the fraction on the reverse strand, the dominant monomer class (most frequent monomer_class) and the family: majority family_id for existing arrays, or for new arrays the famnew family of (array, dominant class), else 'new:<array>'. The run's own GC (gc_of) and the consensus GC of the dominant class are stored for gate G1. The unit length comes from the 02 table and sets the unit class.
inputs: c, s, e, aid (array id), seg (gap segment), src ('existing' or 'new'), C = copies dict from load_copies(); module-level per (array -> period), famnew, cgc, NSEG
outputs: returns dict with chrom, start0, end, bp, source, array_id (<aid>~g<seg> when the array has > 1 gap segment), array_id_v46, gap_segment, unit_bp, unit_class, n_conf, n_weak, n_junk, mean_identity_conf, reverse_fraction, run_GC, consensus_GC ('NA' if unknown), dominant_class, family and hidden helpers _gc_diff, _mid, _rev; or None
rule_or_threshold: copy counted inside the run when copy start >= s and copy end <= e; n_conf: complete and identity >= 80; n_weak: 65 <= identity < 80, or truncated with identity >= 80; n_junk: identity < 65; unit_class <= 6 micro, < 100 mini, else satellite; _gc_diff = |run_GC - consensus_GC|

what_it_does: Decides, per catalogue family, whether the repeated unit is really a tandem gene array (rRNA, 5S rRNA, tRNA, snRNA, miRNA) rather than a satellite. Used as a module by 59_final_catalogue.py (classify() then write()) and as a stand-alone report. Stand-alone flow: (1) argv G, catalogue TSV, overlay folder, output TSV; (2) read the catalogue rows; (3) classify() loads the gene tracks (load_tracks), measures per family the overlap of its runs with every gene class and calls gene_array / gene_related / satellite; (4) write() writes the per-family table and the cut-off sweep; (5) prints the sweep rows and the gene-array families.
inputs: catalogue TSV (family, chrom, start0, end, unit_bp per run); annotation_overlays/<G>: fClaHyb_<G>.rRNA.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.tRNA.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.miRNA.curated.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.rfam.all_classes.sorted.gff3.gz
rule_or_threshold: CUTS = 0.5/0.7/0.8 (observed/expected bp ratio), UCUTS = 0.3/0.5/0.7 (share of units carrying a gene hit); defaults cut 0.7, unit_cut 0.5

what_it_does: Loads the gene annotations of the subgenome and sorts every feature into one gene class: rRNA GFF (barrnap) -> 5S_rRNA when '5S' appears in the attributes else rRNA_other; tRNA GFF (types tRNA, gene, pseudogene) -> tRNA; curated miRNA GFF -> miR-430 when the name matches mir-430 else miRNA_other; Rfam GFF -> snRNA_U1..U6 (Name U1-U6 or U1_...), snRNA_other (type snRNA), 5S_rRNA (5S_rRNA / RF00001), tRNA (tRNA / RF00005), rRNA_other (LSU/SSU/5.8S accessions), miR-430, miRNA_other (names starting mir-/MIR). Within a class, overlapping features on a chromosome are merged so one gene reported by two tracks is counted once. The median merged-feature length per class is recorded as the typical gene length.
inputs: G; OVL = annotation_overlays/<G> folder (files resolved with overlay_path)
outputs: returns (idx = {class: {chrom: sorted merged (start, end)}}, glen = {class: median merged feature length in bp})
rule_or_threshold: GFF coordinates converted to 0-based starts; median gene length defaults to 100 bp when a class has no feature

what_it_does: Returns how many bp of the interval [s, e) are covered by the merged gene features of chromosome c and how many of those features overlap it.
inputs: d = {chrom: sorted merged intervals} for one gene class, c, s, e
outputs: returns (overlap bp, number of overlapping features)
rule_or_threshold: scan starts at the first feature starting >= s - 100,000 bp

what_it_does: For every catalogue family it adds up the family's run bp, the number of runs and the unit lengths, and for every gene class the bp overlapped, the number of overlapping gene features and the number of runs hit. For a family with at least one hit, the top class is the class with most overlapped bp. It then compares the observed bp share of that class with the share expected if every repeat unit carried one gene (expected = min(1, median gene length / bp-weighted median unit)), giving ratio = observed / expected, and the share of units carrying a gene = min(1, number of gene features / (family bp / unit)). Call: gene_array:<class> when ratio >= cut AND unit share >= unit_cut; gene_related:<class> when ratio >= 0.2; else 'satellite_sporadic_genes'. Gene_related families keep element_class satellite but carry the flag. A sweep records bp per call over all cut combinations. Nested call(c_, uc) applies the rule at given cut-offs.
inputs: rows = catalogue dicts (family, chrom, start0, end, unit_bp); G; OVL; cut (default 0.7); unit_cut (default 0.5)
outputs: returns (calls = {family: dict(family, bp, n_runs, unit_bp_median_bpw, top_class, top_bp_share, gene_len_median, expected_share_one_gene_per_unit, observed_over_expected, hits_per_unit, unit_share, top_run_share, element_class, gene_flag, call_at_<cut>_u<ucut> x 9, all_classes)}, sweep = list of dict(ratio_cut, unit_cut, Mb per call type))
rule_or_threshold: families with no gene overlap are absent from calls (59 then treats them as satellite, gene_flag none); bp-weighted median unit = unit at which cumulative run bp reaches half the family bp; expected share = min(1, gene_len_median / unit); ratio = observed share / expected share; unit share = min(1, n features / (family bp / unit)); gene_array if ratio >= cut (0.7) and unit share >= unit_cut (0.5); gene_related if ratio >= 0.2; element_class = gene_array:<class> or satellite; gene_flag = the call, or none for satellite_sporadic_genes; sweep over 0.5/0.7/0.8 x 0.3/0.5/0.7

what_it_does: Writes the per-family gene-array table and the cut-off sweep table next to it.
inputs: calls and sweep from classify(); out = output TSV path
outputs: <out> (one row per family with the columns listed under classify); <out with .tsv replaced by _sweep.tsv> (ratio_cut, unit_cut, gene_array, gene_related, satellite_sporadic_genes in Mb; missing call types written as 0.0)
rule_or_threshold: per-family table written only when at least one family has a gene hit

what_it_does: Library module with no command-line flow: one resolver for the functional-annotation folder layout, imported by 59_final_catalogue.py, 59b_gene_arrays.py, 59c_te_layer.py and 59e_interruptions.py. The annotation folders were renamed in 2026-10 from <FUNC>/_repeats_EDTA/ to <FUNC>/fClaHyb_<G>_repeats_EDTA/; every function tries the new layout first, then the old one, and raises instead of guessing when the file is missing.
inputs: FUNC root folder, subgenome tag g, sub-folder suffix, file name

what_it_does: Finds an annotation file under the functional-annotation root: first <func>/fClaHyb_<g><sub>/<name> (current layout), then <func>/<sub>/<name> (pre-2026-10 layout). Returns the first that exists; when none exists it raises FileNotFoundError (required=True) or returns None.
inputs: func, g, sub (e.g. '_repeats_EDTA'), name, required (default True)
outputs: returns path string or None; raises FileNotFoundError

what_it_does: Same as func_path for a folder: returns <func>/fClaHyb_<g><sub> if it is a directory, else <func>/<sub>; raises FileNotFoundError when neither exists.
inputs: func, g, sub

what_it_does: Finds a file in the annotation_overlays folder: first <ovl>/<name>, then <ovl>/<g>/<name> (when the parent folder was given). Raises FileNotFoundError when missing and required, else returns None.
inputs: ovl = annotation_overlays/<G> (or its parent), g, name, required (default True)
outputs: returns path or None; raises FileNotFoundError

what_it_does: Returns the path of the chromosome-level genome FASTA of subgenome g through func_path (sub-folder _genome, file fClaHyb_<g>_LG.fa).
inputs: func, g

what_it_does: Returns the path of the assembly-gap BED of subgenome g through func_path (sub-folder _genome, file fClaHyb_<g>_LG.gaps.detgaps.bed).
inputs: func, g

what_it_does: Measures the transposable-element (TE) content of every catalogue run while separating EDTA labels that merely describe the satellite itself (EDTA calls many satellites TE) from real TE insertions inside the array. All work is at module top level. Flow: (1) argv G, catalogue TSV, pipeline out folder, new-array 03 folder or '-', functional annotation root, step-54 insertion folder, optional destination (default = the catalogue's folder); (2) read the catalogue; rows carried from an earlier catalogue (carried_from != none) are skipped and counted; (3) load the confident copies (complete, identity >= 80) of the needed arrays, looked up by array_id_v46, from the existing and new 03_monomer_copies.tsv; duplicates removed; (4) read the EDTA TE GFF (repeat_region / target_site_duplication / long_terminal_repeat records excluded); label = the 'classification' attribute or the feature type; (5) read the step-54 known-TE families (54c_ins_families_classified.tsv, class known_TE) and the genomic locations of their members (54b_ins_members.tsv, ins_id = '<G>|...|chrom:start-end'); (6) per run: collect the EDTA features overlapping it, group them by label; for each label the carried share = fraction of the run's confident copies that at least one feature of that label covers by >= 50 % (of the copy length by default, or of min(copy, feature) with SATCHAIN_59C_CARRY=min); EDTA_overlap_bp = clipped union of all overlapping features; for each intrinsic cut 0.2/0.3/0.5: labels with carried share > cut are 'intrinsic' (the label describes the satellite), the remaining features are TE insertions -> TE_insert_bp_<cut> (clipped union) and TE_insert_n_<cut>; missed known-TE insertions of step 54 starting inside the run are counted and summed; (7) write <dest>/59c_te_<G>.tsv and print a summary per intrinsic cut. Nested clipped(xs) = bp of the union of intervals clipped to the run.
inputs: CAT = 59_catalogue_<G>.tsv; OUT/fClaHyb_<G>_satellites/03_monomer_copies.tsv; N03/03_monomer_copies.tsv; FUNC/.../fClaHyb_<G>.TEanno.sorted.gff3.gz (func_path); INS/54c_ins_families_classified.tsv; INS/54b_ins_members.tsv; env SATCHAIN_59C_CARRY (copy|min)
outputs: <dest>/59c_te_<G>.tsv (run_id, chrom, start0, end, bp, family, seq_cluster, element_class, EDTA_overlap_bp, labels_carried (top 4 label:share), intrinsic_labels_<cut>, TE_insert_bp_<cut>, TE_insert_n_<cut> for cut 0.2/0.3/0.5, missed_TE_insertions_54, missed_TE_bp_54); printed summary per cut (runs, satellite Mb, EDTA overlap Mb, TE insertion Mb and fraction, runs with insertions, runs with intrinsic labels) and missed-TE line
rule_or_threshold: confident copy = complete AND identity >= 80; a copy 'carries' a label when one feature of that label overlaps >= 50 % of the copy (RULE copy, default) or >= 50 % of min(copy length, feature length) (RULE min, v4.6); carried share = carrying copies / confident copies; intrinsic label when carried share > cut, cuts 0.2, 0.3, 0.5; assertion fails when a run of source existing/new with n_conf > 0 has no matching copy; missed_TE_bp_54 = sum over step-54 known-TE members starting inside the run of (min(run end, member end) - member start)

what_it_does: Gives every new-array run a family (grouping unmatched new consensuses into NewSat families) and every satellite family a satellitome name, then recomputes the tiers. All work is at module top level. Flow: (1) argv G, catalogue folder, new-array folder or '-'; name prefix Cga for Gar, Cma for Mac; (2) read 59_catalogue_<G>.tsv; (3) when <N>/famnew.tsv exists: read (array_id, monomer_class) -> family; read the all-vs-all BLAST of new consensuses (<N>/new_allvsall.tsv) and link two consensuses whose families are both unmatched ('new:') when identity >= 80 % and alignment length >= 50 % of the shorter consensus (single linkage with a union-find; nested find(x) returns the group root with path compression); groups ranked by size get names NewSat<G><5-digit rank>; (4) per run: family_v46 = for a new, not carried run: the NewSat name of (array_id_v46, dominant_class) if any, else the famnew family of that pair, else the catalogue family; for every other run family_v46 = family; (5) bp and unit lengths summed per family_v46 over satellite-class runs; tiers recomputed on the cumulative share; (6) satellite families ranked by bp: name_v46 = <Cga|Cma>Sat<rank, 3 digits>-<median unit bp>; non-satellite runs get name_v46 = '<element_class>|<family_v46>' and tier 'gene_array'; (7) 59_catalogue_<G>.tsv rewritten in place with family_v46, name_v46 and updated tier; 59d_names_<G>.tsv written; 59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv rewritten on family_v46; summary printed.
inputs: <C>/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv; <N>/famnew.tsv (array_id, monomer_class, family); <N>/new_allvsall.tsv (BLAST tabular: query, subject, pident, length, ..., qlen, slen; ids 'array|class')
outputs: <C>/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv (rewritten; adds family_v46, name_v46; tier updated); <C>/59d_names_<G>.tsv (name_v46, family_v46, bp, share, unit_bp_median, tier, seq_cluster, n_runs); <C>/59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv (family, bp, share, tier, seq_cluster, element_class; rewritten)
rule_or_threshold: BLAST link: pident >= 80 and length >= 0.5 x min(qlen, slen), self hits ignored, only pairs where both families start with 'new:'; NewSat groups ordered by member count; dominant_class missing -> 'C01'; tiers on satellite-class bp: core while cumulative share before the family < 0.5, major < 0.9, minor < 0.99, rare; rank printed with 3 digits (plain number beyond 999); median unit = middle element of the sorted unit list

what_it_does: Classifies the interruption (the stretch of sequence) between two neighbouring catalogue runs of the same family: is it a TE insertion, a known-TE insertion missed by EDTA, a gene feature, an SSR, or unannotated. Flow: (1) parse arguments G, catalogue folder, functional annotation root, step-54 insertion folder and options; (2) read the catalogue runs of element_class satellite (all classes with --all-classes); family = family_v46 when present else family; (3) read 59c_te_<G>.tsv to get, per run and per intrinsic cut, the EDTA labels that describe the satellite itself; (4) build a Gaps object from --gaps or env SATCHAIN_GAPS when given; (5) read the EDTA TE GFF (label = classification attribute; repeat_region / TSD / LTR records excluded); (6) read other annotations: LiftOn exon+CDS and gene spans, ncRNA from the Rfam / tRNAscan / barrnap / ncRNA_all GFFs when present (types other than gene and region), SSR from GMATA_SSR bed.gz files under the _TR folder; (7) read the step-54 known-TE insertion members; (8) pairs = consecutive runs of the same (chromosome, family) ordered by start; (9) classify() each pair at --class-cut, --intrinsic-cut (falls back to the smallest cut present in 59c) and --max-gap; pairs separated by an assembly gap or contig join are refused and counted; (10) write 59e_interruptions_<G><suffix>.tsv and print the class summary, refused count, across-array count and the top TE labels; (11) with --sweep write 59e_sweep_<G><suffix>.tsv over class-cut 0.3/0.5/0.7 x every intrinsic cut in 59c x max-gap 10/20/50 kb.
inputs: <C>/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv; <C>/59c_te_<G>.tsv; FUNC/.../fClaHyb_<G>.TEanno.sorted.gff3.gz; FUNC/.../fClaHyb_<G>.lifton.sorted.gff3.gz; optional fClaHyb_<G>.rfam.all_classes / .tRNA / .rRNA / .ncRNA_all .sorted.gff3.gz; FUNC/.../_TR/GMATA_SSR/fClaHyb_<G>.SSR.*.bed.gz; INS/54c_ins_families_classified.tsv; INS/54b_ins_members.tsv; --gaps BED or env SATCHAIN_GAPS
outputs: <C>/59e_interruptions_<G><suffix>.tsv (subgenome, family, array_left, array_right, array_relation, chrom, start0, end, bp, run_left, run_right, TE_frac, missed_TE54_frac, exon_CDS_frac, intron_frac, ncRNA_frac, SSR_frac, class, top_TE_label); optional <C>/59e_sweep_<G><suffix>.tsv (class_cut, intrinsic_cut, max_gap, n, Mb, class, n_class, Mb_class); printed summary
rule_or_threshold: defaults: --max-gap 50000 bp, --own 0.8, --min-len 500 bp, --class-cut 0.5, --intrinsic-cut 0.3; sweep: class cut 0.3/0.5/0.7, max gap 10,000/20,000/50,000

what_it_does: Decides whether an EDTA feature is a whole element sitting inside the interruption, in which case it counts as TE even when its label is intrinsic to the flanking satellite runs (EDTA gives e.g. MacSat03 and an LTR element interleaved with it the same label).
inputs: x = (start, end, label) feature; s, e = interruption bounds; module constants MINLEN, OWN
