rule_or_threshold: element length >= --min-len (500 bp) AND overlap with the interruption >= --own (0.8) x element length

what_it_does: Returns the number of bp of the interruption [s, e) covered by the union of the intervals of one annotation track on chromosome c. When a skip set of labels is given, features carrying one of those labels are ignored unless own() shows they are whole elements inside the interruption.
inputs: iv = {chrom: sorted intervals (start, end[, label])}, c, s, e, skip = set of intrinsic labels or None
rule_or_threshold: scan starts at the first interval starting >= s - 200,000 bp

what_it_does: Classifies the interruption between left run a_ and right run b: the interval from the end of a_ to the start of b. Returns None when the interval is empty or longer than maxgap, and 'refused' when an assembly gap or contig join lies inside or exactly at its ends. The EDTA labels intrinsic to either flanking run (at intrinsic cut icut) are skipped. It measures the bp covered by non-intrinsic TE, by step-54 known-TE insertions, by exons/CDS, genes, ncRNA and SSR (intron = gene - exon), then assigns one class in priority order: TE_insertion, missed_TE_54, other:<exon_CDS|intron|ncRNA|SSR> (whichever covers most), unannotated. Also reports the TE label with most bp.
inputs: a_, b = catalogue row dicts (end, start0, chrom, run_id, array_id, array_id_v46); cut (class cut), icut (intrinsic cut key), maxgap; module-level te, kte, other, intr, GAPS
outputs: returns a row list [subgenome, family, array_left, array_right, array_relation (same_array if same array_id_v46 else across_arrays), chrom, start0, end, bp, run_left, run_right, TE_frac, missed_TE54_frac, exon_CDS_frac, intron_frac, ncRNA_frac, SSR_frac, class, top_TE_label], or None, or 'refused'
rule_or_threshold: L = end - start; skipped if L <= 0 or L > maxgap; refused if GAPS.between(chrom, start, end, closed=True); TE_insertion if TE bp >= cut x L; else missed_TE_54 if known-TE bp >= cut x L; else other:<type> if the best of exon_CDS / intron / ncRNA / SSR >= cut x L; else unannotated; intron = max(0, gene bp - exon bp)

what_it_does: Command-line sampler that builds the pool of monomer copies used by the k-mer clustering of 55c (pooled across haplotypes in one call). Steps: (1) parse <dest>, <per_run>, optional --all-satellite and one spec per haplotype G=<pipeline out>|<catalogue tsv>[|<new03 dir>]; (2) per haplotype read the catalogue and keep the runs of that subgenome whose element_class is satellite and carried_from is none and (unless --all-satellite) that are flagged candidate centromeric, grouped by array_id_v46; (3) read 03_monomer_copies.tsv of the pipeline output (plus the extra new03 copy table when given), keep complete copies with identity >= 80 whose array is among the kept arrays, skip a tile whose array/start/end equal the previous tile (StringDecomposer batch-overlap duplicates), and attach each copy to the run whose interval contains it; (4) per run draw up to per_run copies with a random generator seeded on the run id so that adding or removing other runs does not change the draw; (5) write the sequence to 55_sample.fa (header <G>|<monomer_id>) and one metadata row to 55_sample.tsv; (6) print copies / runs sampled per haplotype.
inputs: argv: <dest> <per_run> [--all-satellite] G=<out>|<catalogue tsv>[|<new03 dir>] ...; <catalogue tsv> (subgenome, element_class, carried_from, putative_centromeric_array_L1, cen_candidate_ror, array_id_v46, run_id, start0, end, family); <out>/fClaHyb_<G>_satellites/03_monomer_copies.tsv and optional <new03>/03_monomer_copies.tsv (array_id, complete_or_truncated, best_alignment_identity, genomic_start_0based, genomic_end, monomer_id, sequence, chrom, monomer_class, strand)
outputs: <dest>/55_sample.fa; <dest>/55_sample.tsv (copy_id, subgenome, run_id, array_id, family, chrom, start0, end, length, monomer_class, strand, identity, cen_L1, cen_ror); one console line per haplotype
rule_or_threshold: run kept if subgenome == G, element_class == satellite, carried_from == none; default additionally putative_centromeric_array_L1 == yes or cen_candidate_ror == yes (--all-satellite lifts this); copy kept if complete_or_truncated == complete and best_alignment_identity >= 80; copy belongs to a run when run.start0 <= copy start and copy end <= run.end (first matching run); consecutive duplicate tile (same array_id, start, end) skipped; up to per_run copies per run; RNG seed = crc32(run_id)

what_it_does: Scores every sampled monomer copy of 55a against the gene annotation tracks, giving independent evidence for the k-mer clusters of 55c. Steps: (1) load 59b_gene_arrays.py as a module (ga) to reuse its load_tracks and ov helpers; (2) for each G=<annotation_overlays/G> argument build the merged gene tracks of that haplotype (classes 5S_rRNA, rRNA_other, tRNA, snRNA_*, miR-430, miRNA_other); (3) for every row of 55_sample.tsv compute the fraction of the copy's bp covered by each gene class (overlap bp from ga.ov divided by copy length) and the class with the largest fraction; (4) write copy_id, frac_5S, top_class, top_frac to 55_sample_gene_overlap.tsv; (5) print the number of copies scored and how many have >= 30 % of their length annotated 5S.
inputs: argv: <lin55 dir> G=<annotation_overlays/G> ...; <lin55 dir>/55_sample.tsv (copy_id, subgenome, chrom, start0, end); gene tracks returned by 59b_gene_arrays.load_tracks(G, OVL)[0]
outputs: <lin55 dir>/55_sample_gene_overlap.tsv (copy_id, frac_5S, top_class, top_frac); console count
rule_or_threshold: frac_class = overlap bp / max(1, copy length), rounded to 3 decimals; top_class = none when the largest fraction is 0; console count = copies with frac_5S >= 0.3

what_it_does: Clusters the sampled monomer copies by k-mer composition and chooses how many clusters (K) to report; the clusters are sequence groups, not lineages. Steps: (1) parse <lin55 dir>, --kmax (8), --ari (0.8); read 55_sample.tsv (metadata), 55_sample.fa (sequences) and, when present, 55_sample_gene_overlap.tsv (frac_5S per copy); (2) build the 20-dimensional feature matrix with feats(k) for k = 5, 6, 7; (3) for every k and every K = 2..kmax run kmeans twice with two different seeds and record the silhouette, the ARI between the two restarts and the cluster sizes; (4) for each haplotype with at least 2K copies cluster that haplotype alone and record the ARI between the pooled labels restricted to the haplotype and its own clustering (haplotype stability); (5) for each (k, K) compute the ARI against the k = 6 partition at the same K (stability across k); (6) K choice rule: per K take the minimum cross-k ARI, the minimum restart ARI and the mean silhouette over k; K passes when both ARIs >= --ari and the silhouette is within 10 % of the best mean silhouette over all K; chosen K = the largest passing K >= 3, otherwise K = 2 marked fallback_K2; (7) write 55_K_choice.tsv (with the rule as a trailing comment line), 55_cluster_summary.tsv (per k, K and cluster C<K>.<rank>: n, Gar, Mac, median length, median frac_5S, share of copies with frac_5S >= 0.3, top 3 families), 55_haplotype_stability.tsv and 55_cluster_assignments.tsv (per copy: chosen K, cluster name at k = 6 and the chosen K, and the raw label at every k, K); (8) print the choice table and the chosen K.
inputs: argv: <lin55 dir> [--kmax 8] [--ari 0.8]; <lin55 dir>/55_sample.tsv, 55_sample.fa, optional 55_sample_gene_overlap.tsv
rule_or_threshold: k = 5, 6, 7; K = 2..kmax (8); 20 SVD dimensions; 50 k-means++ starts; seeds 55 + k and 1055 + k; silhouette on 2,000 copies with seed 7; per-haplotype clustering only when the haplotype holds >= 2K copies; K passes when min ARI across k >= 0.8 and min ARI between restart seeds >= 0.8 and mean silhouette >= 0.9 x best mean silhouette; chosen K = largest passing K >= 3, else fallback K = 2; cluster name C<K>.<rank by size>; frac_5S >= 0.3 share reported

what_it_does: Turns every sampled monomer copy into one k-mer composition profile for a given k: counts each k-mer of the copy (skipping k-mers that contain N), merges a k-mer with its reverse complement so that strand does not matter, converts counts to frequencies, takes the square root (Hellinger transform), centres each column, and reduces the copies x k-mers table to 20 coordinates per copy with a randomised truncated SVD. Returns the matrix in which the copies are clustered.
inputs: k (int); module-level ids (copy ids in 55_sample.tsv order) and seqs (sequences read from 55_sample.fa)
outputs: numpy array n copies x 20 dimensions (float64)
rule_or_threshold: canonical k-mer = min(k-mer, reverse complement); k-mers containing N skipped; frequency = count / total k-mers of the copy; sqrt then column centring; TruncatedSVD n_components = 20, random_state = 55, algorithm randomized, n_iter = 7

what_it_does: Partitions the copies in the reduced k-mer space into K clusters with scikit-learn k-means run from 50 k-means++ starting points (the lowest-inertia solution is kept), then renumbers the clusters by size so that label 0 is the largest cluster, 1 the next, and so on. Returns one cluster label per copy.
inputs: Z (n x 20 feature matrix), K (number of clusters), rng (numpy Generator used to draw the sklearn random_state), restarts (50)
outputs: numpy array of integer cluster labels per copy (0 = largest cluster)
rule_or_threshold: n_init = 50 k-means++ starts; max_iter = 300; random_state = rng.integers(2^31); labels ranked by cluster size

what_it_does: Measures how well separated the clusters are on a random subsample of at most 2,000 copies: for each copy a = mean Euclidean distance to the other copies of its own cluster, b = smallest mean distance to the copies of any other cluster, silhouette = (b - a) / max(a, b); returns the mean over the subsample (near 1 = tight and well separated, near 0 = on the border between clusters, negative = probably in the wrong cluster).
inputs: Z (feature matrix), lab (cluster labels), rng (numpy Generator), n (2000)
outputs: float mean silhouette (nan when no copy has a cluster mate or fewer than 2 clusters are present in the subsample)
rule_or_threshold: subsample n = 2,000 copies without replacement; a copy alone in its cluster is skipped; s = (b - a) / max(a, b)

what_it_does: Computes the adjusted Rand index between two partitions of the same copies (for example the k = 5 and the k = 6 clusterings): counts pairs of copies that are grouped together in both partitions, subtracts the agreement expected by chance and rescales so that 1 = identical partitions and about 0 = agreement no better than random.
inputs: x, y (two label lists of equal length)
rule_or_threshold: ARI = (sum_ij C(n_ij, 2) - E) / ((sum_i C(a_i, 2) + sum_j C(b_j, 2)) / 2 - E) with E = sum_i C(a_i, 2) x sum_j C(b_j, 2) / C(n, 2); returns 1.0 when the denominator is 0

what_it_does: Assigns every satellite family to one sequence cluster of 55c by a majority vote of its sampled copies. Steps: (1) parse <lin55 dir>, --min-share (0.7), --min-copies (5), --K (0 = use the chosen_K column of the assignments table); (2) read 55_cluster_assignments.tsv and use the label column k6_K<K> (k = 6 at the chosen K); (3) read 55_cluster_summary.tsv and build a descriptor string per cluster at k = 6, K (n, Gar/Mac split, median length, median 5S fraction, top families); (4) count per (subgenome, family) how many sampled copies fall into each cluster C<K>.<label + 1> and how many distinct runs were sampled; (5) the family receives its majority cluster when the majority share >= min_share and at least min_copies copies were sampled, otherwise unassigned (no plurality calls); (6) write 55d_family_cluster.tsv and print the number of families per outcome.
inputs: argv: <lin55 dir> [--min-share 0.7] [--min-copies 5] [--K n]; <lin55 dir>/55_cluster_assignments.tsv (subgenome, family, run_id, chosen_K, k6_K<K>), <lin55 dir>/55_cluster_summary.tsv
outputs: <lin55 dir>/55d_family_cluster.tsv (subgenome, family, seq_cluster, majority_share, n_sampled_copies, n_runs_sampled, cluster_descriptor); console
rule_or_threshold: k = 6 fixed; K = --K or chosen_K; assigned when majority share >= 0.7 and n sampled copies >= 5, else unassigned; cluster name C<K>.<label + 1>; descriptor empty for unassigned

what_it_does: Writes the sequence clusters computed by step 55d into an existing catalogue without rerunning 59 (breaks the old circular order 59 -> 53 -> 55 -> 59). All work is at module top level. Flow: (1) argv G, catalogue folder, 55d_family_cluster.tsv; family -> seq_cluster read for subgenome G; (2) read 59_catalogue_<G>.tsv; each satellite-class run gets seq_cluster = cluster of its family ('none' when absent); non-satellite runs get 'na'; changed rows counted; (3) catalogue rewritten in place; (4) 59_catalogue_<G>.bed rewritten as BED9 with one colour per cluster from an 8-colour palette (grey 150,150,150 for none / na / unassigned); (5) seq_cluster column of 59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv updated the same way; (6) prints the number of changed runs and runs/Mb per cluster.
inputs: <T> = 55d_family_cluster.tsv (subgenome, family, seq_cluster); <C>/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv; <C>/59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv
outputs: <C>/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv (seq_cluster column updated); <C>/59_catalogue_<G>.bed (BED9, name = run_id|family|element_class|seq_cluster|<unit>bp|tier, itemRgb by cluster); <C>/59_family_tiers_<G>.tsv (seq_cluster updated)
rule_or_threshold: cluster lookup by the 'family' column (not family_v46); palette cycles over 8 colours in sorted cluster-name order

what_it_does: Converts the finished 59 catalogue of each haplotype into the runs-of-record tables that the manuscript figures and tables read. All work is at module top level. Flow: (1) parse arguments: catalogue folder, functional annotation root, destination, --tags (default Gar,Mac), --levels, --version (default v4.7); (2) per haplotype h: read 59_catalogue_<h>.tsv with pandas; family = family_v46 when present else family; name = name_v46 else family; unit_class = catalogue unit_class except 'gene_array' for element_class starting with gene_array; build the record table (haplotype, run_id, chrom, start0, end, run_bp = bp, family, unit_bp, unit_class, copies = n_conf, tier 'S1', verdict '<version>_run_of_record', fish_site_ok, source 'SatChain_<version>', array_id, name_v46, seq_cluster, element_class, gene_flag, centromeric_L1 = putative_centromeric_array_L1, cen_candidate_ror, family_tier = catalogue tier, gates_passed, carried_from); with --levels, columns rlvl1/rlvl2 joined from array_levels_<h>.tsv on array_id; (3) write <dest>/<h>/runs_of_record.tsv and runs_of_record.bed (chrom, start0, end, family, run_bp); (4) family_totals.tsv per (family, unit_class): S1_bp = summed run bp, n_S1 = run count, S2/excluded columns set to 0; (5) chrom_totals.tsv per chromosome of the genome .fai: chrom_bp, satellite_bp (unit_class satellite), satellite_frac, n_runs, mini_bp, gene_array_bp; (6) centromere_check.tsv: for each interval of fClaHyb_<h>.centromeres.confidence.bed, the satellite bp inside, support = bp / interval length, verdict, dominant family; (7) one nomenclature row per family; per-haplotype summary printed; (8) <dest>/satellite_family_nomenclature.tsv written for all haplotypes.
inputs: <CAT>/59_catalogue_<h>.tsv; <R0>/fClaHyb_<h>/fClaHyb_<h>_genome/fClaHyb_<h>_LG.fa.fai; <R0>/fClaHyb_<h>/fClaHyb_<h>_centromeres_satellites/fClaHyb_<h>.centromeres.confidence.bed (optional); --levels/array_levels_<h>.tsv (optional; array_id, rlvl1, rlvl2)
outputs: <OUT>/<h>/runs_of_record.tsv; <OUT>/<h>/runs_of_record.bed; <OUT>/<h>/family_totals.tsv (family, unit_class, S1_bp, S2_bp, excluded_bp, n_S1, n_S2, n_excluded); <OUT>/<h>/chrom_totals.tsv; <OUT>/<h>/centromere_check.tsv (chrom, cen_start0, cen_end, cen_bp, satellite_bp_inside, support, verdict, dominant_family); <OUT>/satellite_family_nomenclature.tsv (haplotype, family, name, element_class, unit_bp_median, bp, n_runs, seq_cluster)
rule_or_threshold: fish_site_ok = 1 when run bp >= 3000 else 0; every run is tier 'S1' (no S2 / excluded runs: those columns are 0); satellite bp of record = sum of runs with unit_class satellite (overlaps already resolved in 59, so sum = union); centromere verdict: satellite_supported when support >= 0.3, weak when >= 0.05, else unsupported; dominant family = family with most run bp inside the interval; unit_bp_median per family = pandas median

what_it_does: Returns the total number of bp covered by a set of intervals after merging overlaps. unclear: the function is defined but never called anywhere in this script (left over from the v4.6 version).
inputs: iv = list of (start, end)

what_it_does: Entry point calls main(). Flow: (1) parse arguments (--out pipeline folder, --genome FASTA, --runs runs-of-record tsv or --extents-ok, --dest default <out>/53_segmentation, window, merge and segmentation parameters); the script refuses to run on step-02 extents without --extents-ok. (2) read 02_satellite_arrays.tsv (optionally restricted by --arrays); in run mode replace the units by the catalogue runs (array_id column holds the run_id, parent = the step-02 array). (3) read 03_monomer_copies.tsv for the parent arrays: per copy the midpoint, length, identity, confident flag (complete and identity >= 80), family, class, strand and (confident copies only) the sequence; sort by midpoint. (4) class merge per parent array with a seeded generator: for every pair of step-03 classes with enough confident copies, count k-mers that are near-fixed in one class and near-absent in the other at each k; keep the pair separate when that count reaches the threshold, otherwise merge the classes (union-find); log every pair to 53_class_merges.tsv; each copy's state becomes its merged class (plus strand with --state class+strand). (5) read the needed chromosomes from the genome. (6) per unit: sliding windows of W bp with step W/2 plus one last window ending at the run end; when fewer than 2 x --min-seg windows exist, fall back to windows of m consecutive copies; a unit still too short is written as segmentable = no. (7) per window compute window_seq_features (comp, 4-mer profile, period blocks), the label block from the copies whose midpoint lies in the window (count, median length / period, IQR / period, mean identity, confident fraction, dominant class fraction, number of classes, shares of the unit's three largest families) and the topo block with topo(); per unit, SVD of the window 4-mer profiles gives the first --kmer-pcs components; every window is written to 53_window_features.tsv.gz. (8) per feature block (comp, kmer, period, label, topo) z-score with zs() and run binseg(); change points of different blocks within one window of each other are clustered; a cluster is accepted when it holds >= 2 block groups (comp + kmer count as one composition group) and at least one group is label-free, else it is a candidate; every cluster is written to 53_change_points.tsv and comp+kmer-only clusters are counted (the pre-2026-11-01 rule). (9) cut the unit at the accepted boundaries, profile each segment with seg_profile() on the copies whose midpoint lies inside, take the median local period of the windows within W/2 of the segment, and write 53_segments.tsv and 53_segments.bed (BED9 coloured by profile). (10) write per unit the architecture (single_segment, same_profile_segments or multi_profile), window mode, segmentable flag, number of confident copies and minority-strand fraction to 53_array_summary.tsv. (11) write 53_summary.tsv (segment profile counts and Mb, architecture counts, windowing modes, accepted-boundary block combinations, comp+kmer-only share, state definition) and print it.
inputs: argv: --out <pipeline out> --genome <fasta> --runs <runs tsv: run_id, array_id, chrom, start0, end, unit_bp> | --extents-ok [--dest] [--arrays] [--state class|class+strand] [--copy-win 10] [--copy-win-min 4] [--seed 53] [--min-win-bp 1000] [--win-units 20] [--max-win-bp 60000] [--kmer-pcs 5] [--penalty 3.0] [--min-seg 3] [--merge-ks 5,6,7,8,10,12,14,16,20] [--merge-pin 0.9] [--merge-pout 0.1] [--merge-min-diag 5] [--merge-min-copies 20] [--merge-sample 400]; <out>/02_satellite_arrays.tsv; <out>/03_monomer_copies.tsv; genome FASTA
rule_or_threshold: see main row; segment profile cut-offs in seg_profile; window needs >= 50 valid bp for sequence features and >= 1 copy for label features; PCA of 4-mer profiles needs >= 3 windows with complete profiles

what_it_does: Reads a genome FASTA and keeps only the chromosomes named in need, as raw byte strings; all other chromosomes are skipped to save memory.
inputs: path (genome FASTA), need (set of chromosome names)

what_it_does: Encodes every k-mer of a window as one base-4 integer (A = 0, C = 1, G = 2, T = 3) so that k-mers can be counted and compared quickly; a k-mer that contains any non-ACGT base receives the code -1.
inputs: a (numpy int8 array of base codes, -1 = non-ACGT), k
outputs: numpy int64 array of length len(a) - k + 1 (empty when the window is shorter than k)
rule_or_threshold: code = sum over positions of base x 4^(k - 1 - j); -1 when any base of the k-mer is non-ACGT

what_it_does: Measures how evenly the k-mers of a window are used: Shannon entropy of the k-mer frequencies divided by the largest entropy possible, so that 1 = all k-mers equally frequent (complex sequence) and values near 0 = a few k-mers dominate (simple or highly repetitive sequence).
inputs: codes (k-mer codes from kcodes), k
outputs: float 0..1 (nan when fewer than 2 valid k-mers)
rule_or_threshold: entropy / log2(min(4^k, number of valid k-mers)); codes < 0 ignored

what_it_does: Builds once (cached in the global CANON) a lookup table that maps each of the 256 possible 4-mers to one of 136 canonical 4-mer indices, a 4-mer and its reverse complement sharing the same index; this makes the 4-mer profile independent of strand.
inputs: none (global cache CANON)
outputs: numpy int64 array of 256 entries -> canonical index 0..135
rule_or_threshold: canonical code = min(code, reverse-complement code); 136 classes

what_it_does: Computes the label-free sequence features of one window: GC content, CpG observed/expected ratio, normalised entropies of 1-, 2-, 3- and 5-mers, the canonical 4-mer frequency profile (136 values, later turned into principal components), and the periodicity block: for every 10-mer the distance to its next identical occurrence; the most common distance is the local period, period_strength = share of recurrences within +/- 6 % of that period, strength_at_02 = share within +/- 6 % of the array period from step 02, recur_frac = fraction of 10-mers that recur at all. A window with fewer than 50 valid bases gets only valid_bp.
inputs: a (int8 base codes of the window), period (array period in bp from step 02), k (10)
outputs: tuple (dict with valid_bp, GC, CpG_oe, ent1, ent2, ent3, ent5, recur_frac, local_period, period_strength, strength_at_02; 136-element 4-mer profile or None)
rule_or_threshold: needs >= 50 valid bp; periodicity needs > 20 valid 10-mers; recurrence distances capped at 20,000 bp; distances 0 and 1 ignored; tolerance 0.94-1.06 x period; strength_at_02 only when period >= 2

what_it_does: Finds change points along a series of windows by binary segmentation: it searches for the single split of a stretch that most reduces the within-segment sum of squares of the z-scored features, accepts the split when the reduction exceeds a penalty, and then repeats inside each half. Returns the window indices at which the feature profile changes.
inputs: X (n windows x d features, z-scored), pen (--penalty), minseg (--min-seg)
outputs: sorted list of change-point window indices
rule_or_threshold: no split when n < 2 x minseg; split accepted when gain > pen x d x log(n) (pen default 3.0); every segment >= minseg windows (default 3); cost = sum of squares minus squared sum / length

what_it_does: Prepares one feature block for the change-point search: replaces missing values by the column median, drops columns that do not vary, and z-scores the remaining columns (subtract the mean, divide by the standard deviation) so that every feature weighs the same.
inputs: M (list of per-window feature rows, may contain nan)
outputs: numpy array n x d' (columns with sd <= 1e-9 removed; n x 0 when none remain)
rule_or_threshold: nan -> column median; keep columns with sd > 1e-9

what_it_does: Summarises the local transition graph of a sequence of copy states (merged step-03 classes in genomic order; None = non-confident copy, ignored): the fraction of transitions that stay in the same state (self-loop), the order-1 entropy of what follows each state, the (AB)n alternation share (fraction of consecutive triples where the first and third states are equal and differ from the middle one) and the number of distinct transition types per transition (edge diversity).
inputs: labels (list of states per copy, None allowed)
outputs: tuple (selfloop fraction, transition entropy in bits, alternation fraction, edge diversity); all nan when there is no transition
rule_or_threshold: a transition with None on either side is dropped; alternation = share of triples with x == z and x != y (nan when no triple)

what_it_does: Classifies one segment from the copies whose midpoint lies in it, in this order: too_short (fewer than 10 copies), unresolved (fewer than 10 confident copies or confident fraction below 0.3), interleaved_families (at least 2 families each holding >= 20 % of the confident copies), alternating (alternation >= 0.5), variant_mixed (class self-loop < 0.6), otherwise homogeneous_monomeric; also reports the dominant family and its share.
inputs: cs (list of copy dicts with conf, fam, cls)
outputs: tuple (profile, dominant family, dominant family fraction, n copies, n confident copies, selfloop, alternation)
rule_or_threshold: too_short: < 10 copies; unresolved: < 10 confident or confident fraction < 0.3; interleaved_families: >= 2 families each >= 20 % of confident copies; alternating: alternation >= 0.5; variant_mixed: selfloop < 0.6; else homogeneous_monomeric

what_it_does: Formats a value for the output tables: None or nan become NA, floats are rounded to n decimals, everything else passes through unchanged.
inputs: x (value), n (decimals, 4)
rule_or_threshold: round to 4 decimals by default

what_it_does: Runs the whole segmentation of the catalogue runs (the numbered flow is in the __script__ row): parses the arguments, loads the units and their monomer copies, merges near-identical step-03 classes per parent array, builds sliding windows inside each run, computes the five feature blocks per window, runs binary segmentation per block, accepts a boundary only when two block groups agree and one of them is label-free, profiles the resulting segments and writes every 53_* table.
inputs: see __script__ row
rule_or_threshold: confident copy = complete and identity >= 80; class merge: k in 5,6,7,8,10,12,14,16,20; k-mer diagnostic when present in >= 0.9 (--merge-pin) of one class's sampled copies and <= 0.1 (--merge-pout) of the other's; classes separate when max diagnostic count over k >= 5 (--merge-min-diag), else merged; only classes with >= 20 confident copies tested (--merge-min-copies); <= 400 copies sampled per class (--merge-sample); RNG seed crc32(array_id) ^ 53; window W = min(60000, max(1000, 20 x period)) bp, step W/2, extra last window ending at the run end; copy-window fallback m = 10 down to 4 copies, step m // 2; segmentable needs >= 2 x 3 windows; 5 k-mer principal components; binseg penalty 3.0 x d x log n, min segment 3 windows; change points of different blocks within +/- 1 window form one cluster at the median index; accepted when >= 2 block groups (comp + kmer = one composition group) and at least one group is label-free (composition or period)

what_it_does: Entry point calls main(). Flow: (1) parse arguments (--out pipeline folder, --run step-53 folder, --func annotation folder, --overlays, --genome-tag, --runs runs-of-record or --extents-ok, --gaps BED default from satpaths, --dest default <run>/53b, --allow-missing layers, seeds and thresholds) and load the assembly-gap BED into a Gaps object (the file must exist). (2) read 53_segments.tsv (segments per unit, optionally restricted by --arrays) and the runs of record (or 02_satellite_arrays.tsv in extents mode); rebuild the class merges of 53_class_merges.tsv with union-find. (3) read 03_monomer_copies.tsv for the parent arrays: start, end, class (or U when not confident), family. (4) load the annotation features with load_annotations(). (5) per run, with a generator seeded on the run id: take the copies whose midpoint lies in the run; dominant family = the most common family among confident copies; rank the merged classes of the dominant family by copy count into V1, V2, V3, Vx and write the rank-to-class map to 53b_state_map.tsv; each copy's state = U (not confident), OF (other family) or its rank. (6) intrinsic annotations: for every label compute the share of confident copies it covers; above --intrinsic-frac the label describes the satellite itself and is classed uniform, regional or copy; uniform and regional labels are removed from the feature list (recorded as an attribute), copy-scale labels stay as cross-tags. (7) build_path() for the whole run. (8) for the unit array (the whole run) and for each step-53 segment: restrict the path to the unit, run stats() on the full path and on the variant-only path (non-variant states become breaks) to fill the var_* columns, run order2() on the variant-only path, write the transition counts to 53b_transitions.tsv. (9) core/accessory edges: among the segments with enough transitions and an informative profile, a major edge is a transition that is frequent within its row; edges present in every such segment are core, the others accessory (53b_core_accessory_edges.tsv). (10) write one row per unit to 53b_topologies.tsv with D_trans and D_comp versus the whole run and versus the next segment plus the intrinsic annotation string. (11) for qualifying segments compute the split-half null (D between the first and second half of the path, and between odd and even transitions) on the coarse alphabet and add the segment to the pool. (12) write every pool pair to 53b_segment_pairs.tsv, the split-half and nearest-neighbour distances to 53b_library_null.tsv, and for each quantile cut of the split-half null run average-linkage clustering of the pool and label the topology types T01, T02 ... by size in 53b_topology_library.tsv; print a summary line.
inputs: argv: --out <pipeline out> --run <53 dir> --func <annotation folder> --overlays <dir> --genome-tag <G> --runs <runs tsv> | --extents-ok [--gaps bed] [--dest] [--arrays] [--allow-missing EDTA,Rfam,SSR,rRNA,tRNA,miRNA,gene,SINE] [--seed 53] [--perms 200] [--order2-sims 100] [--min-trans 40] [--intrinsic-frac 0.3] [--uniform-frac 0.95] [--copy-scale 2.0] [--major-p 0.15] [--major-n 5] [--lib-null-quantiles 0.5,0.9,0.95,0.99] [--null-split halves|alternate] [--max-gap-frac 0.5]; <run>/53_segments.tsv; <run>/53_class_merges.tsv; <out>/03_monomer_copies.tsv; <out>/02_satellite_arrays.tsv (extents mode); detgaps BED; annotation layers listed in load_annotations
rule_or_threshold: see main row

what_it_does: Opens a text file for reading, transparently decompressing it when the name ends in .gz.
inputs: p (path)

what_it_does: Shannon entropy in bits of a count table (for example the number of copies per state): 0 when only one state is present, larger when many states are equally common.
inputs: c (Counter of counts)
rule_or_threshold: H = -sum p log2 p; 0 for an empty table

what_it_does: Jensen-Shannon divergence in bits between two count tables after normalising each to frequencies: 0 = identical composition, 1 = no state in common. Used as D_comp (composition difference between two units) and per state inside D_trans.
inputs: p, q (Counters)
rule_or_threshold: JSD = (KL(P||M) + KL(Q||M)) / 2 with M = (P + Q) / 2; empty table treated as total 1

what_it_does: Converts an EDTA feature type string into one coarse TE state label by keyword search in a fixed order: Gypsy, Copia, LTR, LINE, SINE, Helitron, DNA / TIR / MITE (all -> TE:DNA), fragment; anything else becomes TE:other.
inputs: s (GFF3 type column, possibly prefixed 'x|type,...')
rule_or_threshold: first keyword hit in the listed order, case-insensitive

what_it_does: Loads every annotation layer that may become a state of the path, for the chromosomes of the units: EDTA TEs (skipping repeat_region, target_site_duplication and long_terminal_repeat, labelled by te_label), Rfam ncRNAs (rRNA/tRNA/miRNA names skipped; snRNA when the type is snRNA or the name starts with U, else ncRNA:<type>), GMATA SSR beds (di, tri, tetra, penta_hexa), barrnap rRNA (5S or rRNA), tRNAscan tRNA, curated miRNA, LiftOn CDS and exon, AnnoSINE SINE bed. Each layer is located with satpaths (current fClaHyb_<G>_<layer> layout, then the overlays folder); a missing layer stops the run unless it is named in --allow-missing. Returns per chromosome a sorted list of features with a unique id (layer:chrom:start-end).
inputs: a (parsed args: func, overlays, genome_tag, allow_missing), chroms (set of chromosome names); files per the LAYERS table: fClaHyb_<G>.TEanno.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.rfam.all_classes.sorted.gff3.gz, GMATA_SSR/fClaHyb_<G>.SSR.<nm>.bed.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.rRNA.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.tRNA.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.miRNA.curated.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.lifton.sorted.gff3.gz, fClaHyb_<G>.SINE.AnnoSINE.merged.bed.gz
outputs: dict chrom -> sorted list of (start0, end, label, feature id)
rule_or_threshold: GFF start converted to 0-based; features with end <= start dropped; tRNA types tRNA / gene / pseudogene; miRNA types miRNA / pre_miRNA / miRNA_primary_transcript / gene; gene layer CDS and exon only; missing layer = SystemExit unless listed in --allow-missing

what_it_does: Names an unannotated stretch between two neighbours of the path by its size class.
inputs: L (length in bp)

what_it_does: Asks the Gaps object whether an assembly gap or contig join lies in the stretch a..b of chromosome c, using the closed test (a join exactly at a copy edge counts) when gaps.py supports it, else the plain test.
inputs: gaps (gaps.Gaps), c (chrom), a, b (coordinates)
rule_or_threshold: closed = True when accepted by gaps.between

what_it_does: Turns the copies of one unit plus the overlapping annotation features into one ordered path of states along the chromosome. A feature covering at least half of a copy replaces that copy by the feature label (when several, the one with the lowest priority number wins: TE, then 5S/rRNA, then tRNA/miRNA/snRNA, then ncRNA/SINE, then CDS, exon, SSR); an unused feature lying at least half inside a kept copy tags that copy as a cross-feature (for example V1.SINE) unless the copy is U or OF; the remaining features (except exon) are inserted as nodes of their own; consecutive pieces of one feature, or consecutive overlapping features with the same label, collapse into one state; an unannotated stretch between neighbours longer than max(50 bp, gapfrac x period) becomes an INS:<size> node; an assembly gap or contig join between neighbours or inside an item becomes a break (state None) across which no transition is counted.
inputs: cs (list of (start, end, state) copies, sorted), feats (list of (start, end, label, fid) overlapping the unit, sorted), period, gapfrac (--max-gap-frac), gaps (Gaps or None), chrom
outputs: list of (position, state) tuples; state None = path break
rule_or_threshold: replacement when overlap >= 0.5 x copy length; cross-tag when overlap >= 0.5 x feature length (search window: 50 kept copies before the feature end); INS node when stretch > max(50, gapfrac x max(1, period)); CDS/exon tags folded to their base name; exon features never inserted standalone; GAP labels never tagged

what_it_does: Second-order (Miga) test on a path: does the next state depend on the previous two states rather than on the previous one alone? It splits the path at breaks into unbroken runs of more than 2 states, computes gain = H(next | previous) - H(next | previous two) in bits, then simulates sims paths from the path's own first-order transition matrix (same run lengths and start states) to obtain the gain expected from a memoryless chain; reports the observed gain, the null mean, their difference (excess), a z-score, and the two-state context with the strongest second-order effect.
inputs: path (list of (position, state)), rng (random.Random), sims (--order2-sims)
outputs: dict order2_gain_bits, order2_null_bits, order2_excess_bits, order2_z, order2_top_context (all NA when the path has no state triple)
rule_or_threshold: runs shorter than 3 states dropped; sims default 100; z = (gain - null mean) / null sd, NA when sd <= 1e-6; top context needs >= 10 occurrences of the (previous two) pair and is scored by n x KL(observed next given pair || first-order next given last state)

what_it_does: Summarises one unit's state path as a first-order Markov chain: state composition, transition counts (not across breaks), entropy of the composition, entropy rate H(next | current), memory MI = H(next) - H(next | current), the observed versus expected share of stay transitions (same state twice in a row) and the structure index S = (stay_obs - stay_exp) / (1 - stay_exp) (+1 = pure blocks, 0 = no memory, below 0 = alternation), with z-scores of MI and stay against perms shuffles of the path's own states (composition kept, order destroyed, run lengths kept), plus the share of annotation states and a composition string.
inputs: path (list of (position, state)), rng (random.Random), perms (--perms; 0 = no shuffles)
outputs: tuple (dict with n_states, n_trans, n_breaks, entropy_bits, entropy_rate_bits, memory_MI_bits, memory_null_bits, memory_excess_bits, memory_z, size_flag, stay_obs, stay_expected, structure_index, structure_z, annotation_frac, composition; transition Counter; composition Counter)
rule_or_threshold: stay_exp = sum_i row_i x col_i / N^2; size_flag small_n when N < 40 transitions; structure_index NA when stay_exp >= 1; structure_z NA when null sd <= 1e-3 or stay_exp >= 0.95; memory_z NA with fewer than 2 distinct null values; annotation state = any state whose base is not V* and not U or OF; perms default 200

what_it_does: Maps a detailed state name to the coarse library alphabet used to compare segments across units: V1, V2, V3+ (other variants), U, OF, SSR, SINE, TE, INS, gene (CDS/exon), ncRNA (5S, rRNA, tRNA, snRNA, miRNA, ncRNA:*), other; cross-feature tags after the dot are dropped.
inputs: s (state string)

what_it_does: Re-counts a transition table and a composition table on the coarse alphabet of coarse().
inputs: tr (Counter (from, to) -> count), comp (Counter state -> count)
outputs: tuple (coarse transition Counter, coarse composition Counter)

what_it_does: Transition-structure distance between two units on a shared state space: for every state that occurs as a from-state in both units, the Jensen-Shannon divergence of its next-state distributions, weighted by the mean of the two stationary frequencies of that state; 0 = the same states lead to the same next states, 1 = completely different.
inputs: t1, c1 (transition and composition Counters of unit 1), t2, c2 (unit 2)
outputs: float rounded to 4 decimals, or 'NA' when the units share no from-state
rule_or_threshold: w_i = (c1_i / n1 + c2_i / n2) / 2; rows absent in either unit skipped; D = sum w_i x JSD_i / sum w_i

what_it_does: Runs the topology comparison for every catalogue run and its step-53 segments (numbered flow in the __script__ row): loads runs, class merges, copies and annotation layers, builds a state path per run, computes first-order chain statistics, variant-only statistics and the second-order test per unit, writes transition tables, core/accessory edges, per-unit distances to the whole run and the next segment, the split-half null and the topology library.
inputs: see __script__ row
rule_or_threshold: confident copy = complete and identity >= 80 (else state U); variant ranks V1, V2, V3 then Vx; intrinsic label when carried by > 0.3 of confident copies (--intrinsic-frac): uniform when >= 0.95 (--uniform-frac), regional when median feature length > 2.0 x period (--copy-scale), else copy; carried = overlap >= 0.5 x min(copy length, feature length); segments paired and used for edges and the library only when n_trans >= 40 (--min-trans) and profile not unresolved or too_short; major edge = count >= 5 (--major-n) and >= 0.15 of its row (--major-p); split-half D = D_trans (NA counted as 1) + D_comp on the coarse alphabet; library cuts = quantiles 0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99 of the split-half null (--null-split halves by default, alternate = odd/even transitions); average-linkage clustering merges while the mean pairwise D <= cut; RNG seed crc32(run_id) ^ 53; perms 200; order2 sims 100; INS threshold max(50 bp, 0.5 x period)

what_it_does: Entry point calls main(). Flow: (1) parse arguments (--scratch folder with cat53/<G>_<src>/53b/53b_topologies.tsv and cat59/59_catalogue_<G>.tsv, or explicit --topologies G:src=path and --catalogue G=path; --genomes Gar,Mac; --sources existing,new; --min-trans; --q; --excess; --sims; --dest). (2) per genome read the catalogue and aggregate per run_id the family (family_v46 when present), the name and the median unit_bp. (3) per source read 53b_topologies.tsv, keep the unit == array rows (whole runs), rename array_id to run_id, add bp = end - start0 and a default order2_sims, and merge the family columns on run_id. (4) concatenate everything, convert order2_z, order2_excess_bits, memory_z, var_n_trans and n_trans to numbers and compute p_one_sided from order2_z. (5) per genome: testable runs = order2_z defined; for every minimum m the reported set = testable runs with var_n_trans >= m; q-values by bh() within that set (column q_bh_min<m>); for every q cut and excess floor count the hits and their bp and print the line; print the overlap with first-order memory hits, the top families by hit bp and the most frequent top contexts. (6) write 53b_o2_runs.tsv (all run rows with p and q columns) and 53b_o2_sweep.tsv (one row per genome x m x q cut x excess floor).
inputs: argv: --dest <dir> and either --scratch <S> or --topologies G:src=<53b_topologies.tsv> ... --catalogue G=<59_catalogue_G.tsv> ...; [--genomes Gar,Mac] [--sources existing,new] [--min-trans 20,50,100,200] [--q 0.05,0.01] [--excess 0,0.05,0.1] [--sims 100]; 53b_topologies.tsv (unit, array_id, start0, end, order2_z, order2_excess_bits, memory_z, var_n_trans, n_trans, order2_sims, order2_top_context); 59_catalogue_<G>.tsv (run_id, family / family_v46, name_v46, unit_bp)
outputs: <dest>/53b_o2_runs.tsv, <dest>/53b_o2_sweep.tsv (genome, min_transitions_variant_only, q_cut, excess_floor_bits, n_runs, n_testable, n_reported, n_hits, hits_Mb, reported_Mb, n_sims, p_model); console summary
rule_or_threshold: see main row

what_it_does: Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction: sorts the p-values, multiplies each by n / rank, makes the result non-increasing from the largest p downwards and caps it at 1; returns one q-value per p-value in the original order.
inputs: p (array of p-values)
rule_or_threshold: q_(i) = min over j >= i of p_(j) x n / j, capped at 1

what_it_does: Pools the second-order test results of one or more 53b runs over the catalogue runs, converts each run's z into a one-sided p, applies Benjamini-Hochberg within each reported set and counts hits for every combination of minimum chain length, q cut and excess floor (numbered flow in the __script__ row).
inputs: see __script__ row
rule_or_threshold: testable run = unit == array and order2_z defined; reported set at m = var_n_trans >= m for m in 20, 50, 100, 200 (--min-trans); p = 0.5 x (1 + erf(-z / sqrt 2)) (normal tail of a simulation z, stated as an approximation); BH within the reported set; hit = q <= q_cut (0.05, 0.01) and order2_excess_bits >= floor (0, 0.05, 0.1); first-order memory overlap counted at memory_z >= 3; top 8 families by hit bp; --sims 100 fills order2_sims when the column is absent

what_it_does: Library module with no command-line entry (imported by steps 61, 61b, 64 and the benchmarks as the single chain builder). Flow when build_chains(rows, max_gap, min_runs, gaps, keep, satellite_only) is called: (1) group_runs() groups the catalogue rows by array key and sorts them; (2) per array walk the runs in order, test chromosome, distance, family key and assembly gaps against the previous run, extend the chain or flush it; (3) flush drops chains shorter than min_runs and emits one chain record plus one junction record per link; (4) return (chains, junctions, stats).
inputs: catalogue rows (list of dicts), gaps.Gaps object, parameters max_gap, min_runs, keep, satellite_only
outputs: in-memory chains, junctions and stats (no files written)
rule_or_threshold: see build_chains row

what_it_does: Returns the array identity used to group runs into chains: array_id_v46 when the row has a value there, otherwise array_id with any step-59 gap-segment suffix '~g<n>' removed.
inputs: r (catalogue row dict)

what_it_does: Returns the family used to decide whether two runs may be linked: family_v46 when that column exists (even when empty), otherwise family (empty string when absent).
inputs: r (catalogue row dict)

what_it_does: Asks the Gaps object whether an assembly gap or contig join lies between two runs on chromosome c (closed test, a join exactly on a run edge counts, when gaps.py supports it; plain test otherwise).
inputs: gaps (gaps.Gaps), c (chrom), a (left run end), b (right run start)
rule_or_threshold: closed = True when accepted

what_it_does: Groups the catalogue runs by array key and sorts each group by chromosome and start, keeping only satellite runs and, when a keep set is given, only runs whose array_id or array key is in that set.
inputs: rows (catalogue row dicts), keep (set of array ids or None), satellite_only (bool)
outputs: dict array key -> list of rows sorted by (chrom, start0)
rule_or_threshold: satellite_only drops rows with element_class != satellite (a missing column counts as satellite)

what_it_does: Walks the runs of each array in genomic order and links consecutive runs into a chain when they lie on the same chromosome, the spacer between them is between 0 and max_gap bp, they carry the same family key and no assembly gap or contig join lies between them; a refused link closes the current chain and starts a new one. Chains with fewer than min_runs runs are dropped; every link of a kept chain becomes one junction record (left run end, right run start, spacer bp, family on each side). Returns the chains, the junctions and counters of refused links and dropped chains.
inputs: rows (catalogue row dicts with array_id, array_id_v46, family / family_v46, chrom, start0, end, run_id, element_class), max_gap, min_runs, gaps (gaps.Gaps or None), keep, satellite_only
outputs: tuple (chains: list of dict(chain_id, array_id, family, chrom, runs, start0, end, n_runs); junctions: list of dict(chain_id, array_id, family, chrom, gap_index, left_run, right_run, left_end, right_start0, spacer_bp, family_left, family_right, left, right); stats dict with arrays, runs, chains, junctions, runs_in_chains, links_refused_at_gaps, links_refused_family, links_refused_distance, links_refused_chrom, chains_dropped_min_runs)
rule_or_threshold: MAX_GAP = 50,000 bp; MIN_RUNS = 2; link refused in this order of checks: different chromosome, gap < 0 or > max_gap, different family key, assembly gap between the runs (only the first failing reason is counted); chain_id = <array key>#<running index>

what_it_does: Module-level flow: (1) argv <pipeline out> <genome fasta> <tag> <catalogue tsv|-> <TRF bed.gz|-> <out prefix> [n = 300]; both random generators are seeded with 2. (2) read 02_scan_windows.tsv.gz and put every window with a defined period and lag_identity_max into one of the bands 0-0.25, 0.25-0.30, 0.30-0.32, 0.32-0.34, 0.34-0.36, 0.36-0.40, 0.40-1.01. (3) build the null exclusion mask from the intervals of 02_satellite_arrays.tsv, the catalogue runs (start0, end) and the TRF bed entries whose name parses as <unit>bp x<copies> or <motif>x<copies> with unit >= 7 bp; merge overlapping intervals per chromosome. (4) read the whole genome FASTA. (5) per band sample up to n windows, skip windows with more than 10 % N, compute excess() and the best lag. (6) draw up to n random 10-kb windows (chromosomes weighted by length, at most 100 x n attempts) that have <= 10 % N and are not masked, and compute excess() for each. (7) write <out>.tsv (band, band_windows_total, chrom, start, end, scan_period, lag_identity_max, max_excess, best_lag). (8) null p95 = 95th percentile of the null windows' max excess; per band write to <out>_summary.tsv the share of windows with excess >= 0.01, 0.02, 0.05 and above the null p95, the median excess and the null p95; print the summary.
inputs: argv as above; <out>/02_scan_windows.tsv.gz (chrom, start, end, period, lag_identity_max); <out>/02_satellite_arrays.tsv (chrom, start_0based, end); catalogue tsv (chrom, start0, end) or -; TRF bed.gz (name column <unit>bp x<copies> or <motif>x<copies>) or -; genome FASTA
outputs: <out prefix>.tsv (one row per sampled window) and <out prefix>_summary.tsv (tag, band, windows_in_band, sampled, tandem_at_0.01, tandem_at_0.02, tandem_at_0.05, tandem_above_null_p95, median_excess, null_p95); summary printed
rule_or_threshold: bands as listed; n = 300 per band and for the null; windows with > 10 % N skipped; TRF unit >= 7 bp masked; null windows 10 kb outside the mask; tandem cuts 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05 and > null p95; RNG seed 2

what_it_does: Tells whether a candidate null window (chromosome c, s..e) overlaps any excluded interval (step-02 arrays, catalogue runs, TRF calls with unit >= 7 bp), by bisecting the merged exclusion mask of that chromosome.
inputs: c (chrom), s, e (coordinates); module-level mask and starts
rule_or_threshold: looks at the 3 mask intervals starting before e; overlap when an interval end > s

what_it_does: Quantifies tandem repetition in one window: for every 10-mer the distance to its next identical occurrence (lags up to 2,000 bp) gives a lag histogram; the same histogram is computed for a base-shuffled copy of the window (only non-N bases permuted); both are smoothed with a relative window of +/- 6 % of the lag and divided by the number of valid 10-mers; excess = smoothed real minus smoothed shuffled; returns the largest excess over lags >= 7 and the lag at which it occurs (the best lag).
inputs: s (bytes sequence of the window), lmax (2000), k (10); module-level NR generator (seed 2)
outputs: tuple (max excess float, best lag int)
rule_or_threshold: k = 10; lags <= 2,000 bp; smoothing half-width = max(1, round(0.06 x lag)); lags < 7 set to -1 and ignored; shuffle keeps N positions fixed

what_it_does: Module-level flow, one figure per pipeline decision: (1) argv <run folder V> <dest> [--tags Gar,Mac]; set the matplotlib house style (Arial 8 pt, navy ink, no top/right spines). (2) k_choice (banner 7): from lin55/55_K_choice.tsv plot min ARI across k and min ARI between restarts versus K with the 0.8 rule line, mean silhouette with the 0.9 x best line, the chosen K, and stacked cluster sizes at k = 6 from lin55/55_cluster_summary.tsv; the banner sentence hard-codes 'C2.2 = GarSat04 alone, C2.1 = every other family' (not read from a table). (3) gene_arrays (banner 4): per tag a scatter of the families of cat59/59b_gene_arrays_<G>.tsv on the observed/expected bp-share versus unit-share plane with the cut lines, coloured by top gene class, large or named families labelled; the banner names GarSat49, MacSat06 and GarSat04 explicitly. (4) gates (banner 3): per tag bars of the % of runs passing all gates for each setting of cat59/59_gates_sweep_<G>.tsv, the default setting in orange. (5) val56 (banner 2): from hmm56_<G>/val56_benchmark_<G>.tsv the % runs kept, Mb added beyond v4.5 and % of v4.5 bp kept versus q. (6) band_test (banner 1): from benchmarks/threshold_band_test_<G>_summary.tsv the % of windows above the null p95 per lag-identity band, the null level and the old cut. (7) interruptions (banner 6): from cat59/59e_sweep_<G>.tsv stacked Mb per interruption class per sweep setting. (8) order2 (banner 8): from cat53/o2/53b_o2_sweep.tsv at excess floor 0.05 the % of reported runs with order-2 hits versus the minimum number of transitions for q 0.05 and 0.01. (9) te_layer (banner 5): from cat59_minrule/ and cat59/59c_te_<G>.tsv the TE-insertion % of run bp at three intrinsic cuts under the two carry rules. Every banner sentence is filled with numbers computed from the tables at render time; every figure is written by save().
inputs: argv: <run folder> <dest> [--tags Gar,Mac]; <V>/lin55/55_K_choice.tsv, <V>/lin55/55_cluster_summary.tsv, <V>/cat59/59b_gene_arrays_<G>.tsv, <V>/cat59/59_gates_sweep_<G>.tsv, <V>/hmm56_<G>/val56_benchmark_<G>.tsv, <V>/benchmarks/threshold_band_test_<G>_summary.tsv, <V>/cat59/59e_sweep_<G>.tsv, <V>/cat53/o2/53b_o2_sweep.tsv, <V>/cat59_minrule/59c_te_<G>.tsv, <V>/cat59/59c_te_<G>.tsv
outputs: <dest>/bench_k_choice, bench_gene_arrays, bench_gates, bench_val56, bench_band_test, bench_interruptions, bench_order2, bench_te_layer (each .png at 450 dpi + .pdf); console 'wrote <name>' lines
rule_or_threshold: PNG 450 dpi; k-choice reference lines ARI 0.8 and 0.9 x best silhouette; gene-array cut lines ratio 0.7 and unit share 0.5 (dotted 0.2); families labelled when bp > 150,000 or named MacSat06 / GarSat49 / GarSat04; gate default = 5 GC points / identity 85 / band 0.35-0.65; band-test cliff = bands 0.30-0.32 and 0.32-0.34; order-2 panel at excess floor 0.05 with q cuts 0.05 and 0.01; TE panel intrinsic cuts 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5; banner wrap 1.42 mm per character

what_it_does: Applies the house style to one panel: light grid, top and right spines hidden, and an optional left-aligned 9-pt title.
inputs: ax (matplotlib axes), title (string or None)

what_it_does: Draws the numbered-story banner above a figure: a hairline at the top edge, the bold panel number 0.5 mm from the left, the bold one-sentence conclusion (wrapped to the figure width) at 5 mm, a second hairline under the banner, then repacks the panels below it with tight_layout so the banner never covers data.
inputs: fig (matplotlib figure), num (banner number string), text (conclusion sentence)
rule_or_threshold: banner height 7 mm + 3.5 mm per extra wrapped line; wrap width = max(40, (figure width mm - 8) / 1.42) characters; 8 pt bold Arial; 0.5-pt navy hairlines

what_it_does: Writes the figure as <dest>/bench_<name>.png at 450 dpi and <dest>/bench_<name>.pdf (tight bounding box), closes it and prints the name.
inputs: fig, name; module-level D (dest folder)
rule_or_threshold: PNG 450 dpi, white background

what_it_does: Formats a fraction as a whole-number percentage string (0.237 -> '24').
inputs: x (fraction)
rule_or_threshold: 100 x, 0 decimals

what_it_does: Formats the range of a list of values as 'lo-hi' with formatter f (default pct), or as a single value when minimum and maximum format identically; used to fill the numbers in the banner sentences.
inputs: vals (list of numbers), f (formatter)

what_it_does: Reads a tab-separated table into a pandas DataFrame (lines starting with # ignored) or returns None when the file does not exist, so that a missing table simply skips its panel.
inputs: p (path)

what_it_does: Command-line entry for the annotation-free array caller. main() loads the satellite-class rows of the TRF table, then for every chromosome read_fasta -> scan (which calls _acf_counts and _window_call per scan window) -> keeps positive windows -> merges them into array intervals -> attaches overlapping TRF calls and refined boundaries -> writes the array table; then lists TRF satellite calls that no array covers. scan_reference is not called (test oracle only).
inputs: genome FASTA (--genome); 01 TRF table (--trf, only repeat_class==satellite rows kept); --tag; --out; env RUN_ID; optional --win --step --lag-min --lag-max --id-thresh --excess --merge-gap (--threads parsed but unused)
rule_or_threshold: defaults WIN 10000, STEP 5000, lags 40-1000, ID_THRESH 0.34, EXCESS 0.05, MERGE_GAP 20000, TERMINAL_BP 500000; NFFT = next power of two above WIN+LAG_MAX+1

what_it_does: Reads a FASTA file one record at a time and hands back each chromosome name (first word of the header) with its whole sequence in upper case.
inputs: FASTA path

what_it_does: Slow reference version of the periodicity scan kept as a test oracle (not used by main). Slides a 10-kb scan window every 5 kb along a chromosome; if fewer than 80 percent of its bases are A/C/G/T it records a no-call row; otherwise, for every lag k from 40 to 1000 bp, it computes the fraction of positions whose base equals the base k bp further on (only A/C/G/T pairs count) and passes that lag-identity profile to _window_call.
inputs: chromosome sequence string
outputs: list of per-window tuples (start, period, top identity, median identity, harmonic support, primitive period, fft period, top3 lags); no-call = (start,-1,nan,nan,0,-1,-1,())
rule_or_threshold: 10-kb window, 5-kb step; lags 40-1000; valid-base fraction >= 0.80 else no-call

what_it_does: Turns one scan window lag-identity profile into a period call. The period is the lag with the highest identity (top); the background is the median identity over all lags. It then adds three extra period descriptors: harmonic support (how many of lags 2x and 3x period are also elevated), the primitive period (a shorter unit of which the winning lag may be a multiple), an FFT estimate of the spacing between harmonic peaks, and the three best mutually non-adjacent lags.
inputs: window start st; identity vector v over lags; lag vector
outputs: tuple (st, period, top, median, harmonic_support, primitive_period, fft_period, top3)
rule_or_threshold: harmonic: lag 2x or 3x period (<= 1000) elevated if identity > median + 0.4*(top-median); primitive: smallest period/m for m=8..2 (divisible, >= 40) with identity >= median + 0.8*(top-median), else period; FFT: linear detrend, lowest frequency bin >= 2 with power >= 50 percent of max, period = len(v)/bin, -1 if no power; top3: lags differing by > 2 from each other

what_it_does: Fast helper for scan: for a batch of 0/1 indicator rows (one per scan window) it computes, by FFT autocorrelation, how many positions i have a 1 at both i and i+k, for every lag k, and rounds the result back to exact integers.
inputs: 2-D float array (windows x bases) of 0/1 indicators
rule_or_threshold: zero-padded to NFFT so the circular correlation is exact for all lags used

what_it_does: The production periodicity scanner: same statistic as scan_reference but computed in batches of 128 scan windows with FFT. For each window it counts, per lag, the matching A/C/G/T base pairs (sum of the four per-base autocorrelations) divided by the number of valid pairs, giving lag identity; windows with under 80 percent A/C/G/T get a no-call row, the rest go through _window_call.
inputs: chromosome sequence string
outputs: same per-window tuple list as scan_reference
rule_or_threshold: batch 128 windows; valid-base fraction >= 0.80; identity = match counts / max(1, valid pairs)

what_it_does: Runs the whole step. It keeps only satellite-class TRF rows, scans each chromosome, writes every scan window to a sidecar, marks a window positive when its period is real, its top identity is at least ID_THRESH and the excess over background is at least EXCESS, and merges positive windows whose start lies within MERGE_GAP of the previous merged end into one array interval. For each array it records period statistics, copy-number estimate (length/period mode), a repeat class by period, overlapping TRF satellite calls (support, period mode, identity/AT medians), base-pair refined boundaries from same-period TRF calls, terminal/internal status, and QC flags. TRF satellite calls of at least 3 kb that overlap no array are written as orphans and an inventory lists both sets.
inputs: as __script__
rule_or_threshold: positive window: period > 0 and top >= 0.34 and top - median >= 0.05; merge if start - previous end <= 20000; interval = first window start to last window start + 10000; period_mode = most frequent window period; class micro <= 6 bp, mini <= 60 bp, satellite > 60 bp; TRF support = satellite rows overlapping the interval; same-period TRF = |period - mode| <= max(5, 0.15*mode); refined edge: outward at most 5000 bp (one step), inward at most 10000 bp (one window, flagged _clipped_inward); terminal if distance to chromosome end <= 500000; WARN_no_TRF_support if no support; WARN_heterogeneous_period_windows if period range > max(10, 0.10*mode); period_mode_status harmonic_of_shorter_unit if modal primitive period != mode; orphan = TRF satellite >= 3000 bp overlapping no array

what_it_does: Command-line entry for iterative per-array monomer decomposition with StringDecomposer. main() reads the step-02 array table, drops arrays shorter than --min-array-bp, checks/creates a checkpoint, then runs decompose_array for every remaining array (in-process or in a process pool initialised by _worker_init). decompose_array uses _chromseq, finds a seed copy, loops run_sd -> ordered_valid_calls -> nearest_boundary_shift -> cluster_copies (same_class -> circ_match) -> consensus_of, then a final run_sd with the fixed library, and returns per-copy and per-class rows that main writes.
inputs: --genome FASTA (+ faidx_lite index); --arrays 02_satellite_arrays.tsv; --tag; --out; --threads (default 1); --min-array-bp (default 5000); env RUN_ID; external tool stringdecomposer 1.1.2
outputs: 03_monomer_copies.tsv (40 columns, one row per copy); 03_array_consensus.tsv (one row per monomer class); 03_decomposition_iterations.tsv; 03_array_status.tsv; .03_done_arrays.txt checkpoint
rule_or_threshold: constants CLASS_ID 90, CLASS_COV 0.85, LEN_TOL 0.15, MIN_CLASS 8, MAX_CLASSES 12, ORIENT_MARGIN 3.0, PALIN_ID 80, MAX_ITER 5, BOUNDARY_EPS 2 bp, STABLE_ROUNDS 2, MAX_BOOT_BP 150000, CLUSTER_SAMPLE 600

what_it_does: Reverse-complements a DNA string (A/C/G/T/N).
inputs: sequence

what_it_does: Returns the fraction of G or C bases in a sequence (N and other letters count in the denominator).
inputs: sequence

what_it_does: Takes the raw StringDecomposer rows for one array, sorts them by genomic start (then end) so copies stay in array order, and refuses to continue (raises ValueError) if any copy interval is negative, reversed, or runs past the array end.
inputs: list of StringDecomposer rows (fields: read, monomer label, start, inclusive end, identity, ...); array length
outputs: sorted row list; raises ValueError on an invalid interval
rule_or_threshold: interval valid iff 0 <= start <= end < array_length (StringDecomposer end is inclusive)

what_it_does: Measures how much copy boundaries moved between two decomposition rounds: for every copy start of the current round it finds the nearest copy start of the previous round and returns the mean of those distances in bp. Returns None when either list is empty.
inputs: previous starts; current starts

what_it_does: Generator reading a FASTA file record by record (upper case). Not called by main, which uses the faidx_lite index instead.
inputs: FASTA path

what_it_does: Runs the external StringDecomposer program on one array sequence with a monomer library file, single-threaded, optionally asking for the second-best monomer per copy, and returns the rows of its final_decomposition.tsv.
inputs: array FASTA path; library FASTA path; output dir; second_best flag
outputs: list of tab-split rows from final_decomposition.tsv
rule_or_threshold: command: stringdecomposer seq.fa lib.fa -o outdir -t 1 [--second-best]

what_it_does: Compares copy a to copy b allowing any rotation (b is doubled and a is searched as an infix) and either strand, and returns the best identity, a coverage value and the strand that gave it.
inputs: two sequences a, b
rule_or_threshold: identity = 100*(1 - edit distance/len(a)) with edlib HW mode on b+b and rc(b)+rc(b); coverage = min(1, len(a)/len(b))

what_it_does: Decides whether two copies belong to the same monomer class: they must be similar in length, and circ_match must give high identity and coverage.
inputs: two copy sequences
rule_or_threshold: length difference <= 15 percent of the longer; identity >= 90 percent; coverage >= 0.85

what_it_does: Groups copies into monomer classes greedily: copies are taken longest first; each copy joins the first existing class representative it matches by same_class, otherwise it starts a new class. Once 12 classes exist no new class is opened and the copy is forced into the representative with the smallest global edit distance. Classes are returned largest first.
inputs: list of copy sequences
outputs: list of member-index lists sorted by size (desc)
rule_or_threshold: MAX_CLASSES 12; forced assignment by edlib NW edit distance

what_it_does: Builds a class consensus by aligning every member globally to a reference member and taking, at each reference position, the most frequent base among members (N never votes; if the majority is a gap the reference base is kept). Bases inserted relative to the reference are ignored, so the consensus has the reference length.
inputs: member sequences; reference sequence (the middle member)
rule_or_threshold: majority vote per reference column; N excluded; gap majority -> reference base

what_it_does: Per-process initialiser for the pool: opens the faidx index of the genome and stores tag and run id in a module-level dict.
inputs: genome path; tag; run_id

what_it_does: Returns the full sequence of a chromosome from the faidx index, keeping only the most recently used chromosome in memory.
inputs: chromosome name

what_it_does: Decomposes one array into monomer copies and never raises. It cuts the array sequence out of the chromosome, uses the first 150 kb to find a seed: the period-long window (within the first 60 kb, no N in it or the next period) that best matches the next period-length of sequence. The seed is the one-entry library. Up to 5 rounds: StringDecomposer tiles the full array with the library, copies are extracted (reverse-complemented when labelled with an apostrophe), the unresolved fraction and the boundary shift vs the previous round are recorded, and the round is stable when the mean shift is under 2 bp; after 2 stable rounds it stops. Otherwise good copies are sampled, clustered into classes, and a new consensus per class with at least 8 members becomes the library. A final StringDecomposer pass with the fixed library yields the copy rows (strand, orientation margin, phase offset, identity, matches/mismatches/indels, complete vs truncated, AT/GC, sha1) and the class rows (length, GC, copy count, palindromy).
inputs: one 02 array row dict (array_id, chrom, start_0based, end, period_mode_bp); genome via _chromseq; stringdecomposer binary
outputs: dict with status, iters rows (03_decomposition_iterations), cons rows (03_array_consensus), mono rows (03_monomer_copies), nlib
rule_or_threshold: skip if period <= 0 or end <= start (INVALID_PERIOD_OR_INTERVAL); boot = first 150000 bp, need >= 3 periods; seed search step period/4 within first 60000 bp, 2*period window must be N-free; MAX_ITER 5; converged after 2 consecutive rounds with mean boundary shift < 2 bp; good copy for clustering: identity >= 60, |len - period| <= 0.30*period, N <= 5 percent; need >= 8 good copies; sample 600 evenly; class needs >= 8 members; library similarity = mean(1 - HW edit distance/len) when class count unchanged else 0; palindromic if consensus vs its reverse complement identity >= 80; strand_status palindromic / resolved if orientation margin >= 3 points / ambiguous; complete if |copy length - consensus length| <= 15 percent; qc WARN_N_bases if N > 5 percent, PASS if identity >= 70 else WARN_low_identity; status DECOMPOSED / NO_MONOMER_CALLS / FAILED:<exception>

what_it_does: Drives the step: filters arrays by length, builds a fingerprint (sha256 of this script plus every array id/interval/period) that is written at the top of the checkpoint file; if the checkpoint matches and all three output tables exist, already-done arrays are skipped and rows of arrays that were only partly written are trimmed; otherwise old outputs are renamed *.stale and the step restarts. A fresh run also parks the step-04 family outputs as *.stale. Arrays are decomposed sequentially or with a ProcessPoolExecutor, rows are appended and flushed per array, and only non-FAILED arrays are checkpointed so failures are retried on resume. A status table covering every input array is always written at the end.
inputs: as __script__; existing 03 outputs and .03_done_arrays.txt when resuming; previous 03_array_status.tsv
outputs: 03_monomer_copies.tsv, 03_array_consensus.tsv, 03_decomposition_iterations.tsv, .03_done_arrays.txt, 03_array_status.tsv (statuses SKIPPED_BELOW_MIN_ARRAY_BP, DONE_PREVIOUS_CHECKPOINT, DECOMPOSED, NO_MONOMER_CALLS, SKIPPED_*, INVALID_*, FAILED:*); renames *.stale
rule_or_threshold: --min-array-bp 5000; --threads <= 1 runs in-process; pool chunksize 1; progress print every 5 arrays

what_it_does: Command-line entry for descriptive profiles (changes no arrays, copies or families). main() loads the step-02 arrays, step-03 consensuses and copies, step-04 family tables and step-05 symbolic strings; per array it runs composition, shuffled_k7_null and copy_stats, and per monomer class star_profile (variants, conserved windows) and circ_id (identity to the other classes); then it writes family profiles, chromosome and 250-kb TRF summaries from 01_trf_calls_extended.tsv, and, when --centromeres is given, the centromere summary (one row per BED line).
inputs: --genome FASTA (+faidx); --out; --tag; --max-array-bp 500000; --max-copies-per-class 200; --maf 0.10; --conserved 0.95; --window-bp 20; --centromeres BED (optional); --array-id (repeatable filter); files in --out: 02_satellite_arrays.tsv, 03_array_consensus.tsv, 03_monomer_copies.tsv, 04_class_family_assignments.tsv, 04_array_dominant_family.tsv, 05_array_symbolic_strings.tsv, 01_trf_calls_extended.tsv; env RUN_ID
rule_or_threshold: in run_all.sh step 31 the BED is CEN_BED = the centromere=PATH entry of env SAT_OVERLAYS; run_scripts/launch_full.sh sets it to $ANN/fClaHyb_<T>/_centromeres_satellites/fClaHyb_<T>.centromeres.bed with ANN=/mnt/f/data/fClaHyb_func_annotation_v1.0 (file not found at that path on 2026-11-07)

what_it_does: Shannon entropy in bits of a count table (how evenly the counts are spread); NaN when the table is empty.
inputs: collections.Counter

what_it_does: Counts every k-letter word along a sequence, skipping words that contain N.
inputs: sequence; k

what_it_does: Computes array-level sequence features: N fraction, GC and AT fraction, GC skew, entropies of 1-,2-,3-,5-,7-mers, the share of the commonest 7-mer, number of distinct 7-mers, all 16 dinucleotide frequencies and their observed/expected ratios (CpG included), and a low-complexity fraction based on 64-bp windows.
inputs: array sequence (first --max-array-bp bp)
outputs: dict of named features (n_bp, N_fraction, GC_fraction, ..., di_XX, di_oe_XX)
rule_or_threshold: GC skew = (G-C)/(G+C); obs/exp = dinucleotide frequency / (p1*p2); low complexity = non-overlapping N-free 64-bp window with mononucleotide entropy < 1.0 bits or fewer than 12 distinct trinucleotides

what_it_does: Null model for 7-mer entropy: shuffles the A/C/G/T bases of the sequence (same composition) n times and returns the mean and sd of the 7-mer entropy of the shuffles.
inputs: sequence (first 200 kb); n=3; seed=31
rule_or_threshold: 3 shuffles, random seed 31

what_it_does: Aligns each sampled copy globally to its class consensus (edlib, star alignment: every copy against the consensus, not a multiple alignment) and tallies, at every consensus position, how many copies show A, C, G, T or a deletion, and how many copies carry an insertion right after that position.
inputs: class consensus; list of copy sequences
outputs: (count matrix L x 5 [A,C,G,T,del], insertion counts length L+1)

what_it_does: Summarises the step-03 copies of one array: number, copy length mean/sd/cv/mode/min/max, identity mean/sd and divergence (100 - identity) at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles.
inputs: list of 03_monomer_copies rows of one array
rule_or_threshold: divergence = 100 - best_alignment_identity

what_it_does: Percent identity between two consensuses allowing rotation and either strand: x is searched as an infix in y doubled and in reverse-complement y doubled; the smaller edit distance wins.
inputs: sequences x, y
rule_or_threshold: edlib HW mode

what_it_does: Builds all profile tables. Per array: composition on the first 500 kb, shuffled-null z score, copy statistics, reverse and truncated copy fractions, number of classes, dominant-class fraction and an orientation level. Per class: complete copies only, at most 200 sampled (seed 31); from star_profile it writes per-position counts, conservation (top count/aligned) and minor-allele frequency (second count/aligned); positions with MAF at or above --maf become registered variants; runs of at least --window-bp consecutive positions with conservation at or above --conserved become conserved windows (labelled CANDIDATE_NOT_SCREENED); within-class divergence and identity to the other classes of the array are added. Family profiles aggregate consensus length/GC/period per family. From the TRF table it writes per-chromosome counts/bp by period class and, per 250-kb window, the union bp of TRF intervals by interval-length class. CENTROMERE SUMMARY: for every non-comment line of the --centromeres BED whose chromosome exists in the genome, it copies chrom, start and end verbatim as cen_start_0based/cen_end (no selection, no merging: one output row per BED row, so the interval per chromosome is exactly what the BED says), finds the step-02 arrays overlapping that interval, sums overlap bp per dominant family (dominant_satellite_family = family with most overlap bp, secondary = next three), takes period mode/range over the overlapping arrays, counts their step-03 copies, calls orientation mixed if any overlapping array has a step-05 reverse_fraction between 0.35 and 0.65 else uniform, computes AT percent and N count of the centromere segment, carries BED column 5 as centromere_confidence (else NA), and flags every row putative_centromere_not_validated.
inputs: as __script__
rule_or_threshold: array orientation_level: array if reverse fraction <= 0.10 or >= 0.90, else monomer_mixed; class sample <= 200 copies; variant if MAF >= 0.10; conserved window: conservation >= 0.95 over >= 20 bp; TRF period classes micro <= 6, mini 7-60, satellite > 60; 250-kb window interval-length classes 101-500, 501-2000, > 2000 bp; centromere interval = BED columns 1-3 verbatim; overlap test array end > cen_start and array start < cen_end; orientation mixed if any reverse_fraction in (0.35, 0.65); centromere tables only when --centromeres given and no --array-id filter

what_it_does: Command-line entry for copy promotion. main() loads the step-02 arrays, step-03 class consensuses, optional 03c concordance, optional 03d (method C) copies and the step-04 dominant family; it streams 03_monomer_copies.tsv array by array into a nested helper flush() that promotes copies, builds runs, scores each run and assigns an array status; arrays with no copies are added as NOT_DECOMPOSED.
inputs: --out; --tag; --id-sat 75; --id-mini 85; --min-run-copies 10; --max-gap-copies 1; --gc-tol 5; --unit-tol 0.10; env RUN_ID; files in --out: 02_satellite_arrays.tsv, 03_array_consensus.tsv, 03_monomer_copies.tsv, optional 03c_decomposer_concordance.tsv, 03d_monomer_copies_pc.tsv, 04_array_dominant_family.tsv
outputs: 36_monomers_final.tsv (every step-03 copy with promoted flag, reason, run id); 36_arrays_characterized.tsv; 36_characterized_intervals.bed (BED6 of runs); 36_summary.tsv
rule_or_threshold: see main

what_it_does: For each array (nested flush): picks the identity cut-off by unit size, checks whether the median step-03 copy length agrees with the step-02 period, marks each copy promoted when it is complete, reaches the identity cut-off, contains few N and is not N_MASKED (otherwise reason contains_N / truncated / identity<thr); then walks the copies in genomic order building runs of promoted copies that tolerate at most --max-gap-copies demoted copies in a row and contain at least --min-run-copies promoted copies. Each run gets its dominant class and family, a GC check against the class consensus, an orientation check from the reverse fraction, a BED line (score = mean identity x 10, strand - if mostly reverse) and the array gets a status from how much of its scan interval the runs cover. A copy counts as promoted in the output only if it is also inside a run (else isolated_not_in_run).
inputs: as __script__
outputs: 36_monomers_final.tsv, 36_arrays_characterized.tsv, 36_characterized_intervals.bed, 36_summary.tsv (n arrays and Mb by status, copies_total, copies_promoted_in_runs)
rule_or_threshold: identity cut-off: period <= 60 bp -> --id-mini 85, else --id-sat 75; unit agreement: |median copy length - period|/period <= 0.10 else SD_shorter/SD_longer; promoted iff complete AND identity >= cut-off AND N <= 5 percent AND family != N_MASKED; run: <= 1 demoted copy inside (--max-gap-copies), >= 10 promoted copies (--min-run-copies); GC check PASS if |mean copy GC - consensus GC| <= 5; orientation coherent if reverse fraction <= 0.10 or >= 0.90; BED score min(1000, mean identity*10), strand - if reverse fraction >= 0.9; coverage = sum of run lengths / scan interval; status CHARACTERIZED >= 0.5, PARTIAL >= 0.10, no runs and unit disagree -> SHORT_UNIT_UNRESOLVED (period <= 100) or UNIT_DISAGREEMENT_UNRESOLVED, otherwise DIVERGED_UNRESOLVED; no copies -> NOT_DECOMPOSED

what_it_does: Command-line entry for de novo telomere / interstitial telomere (ITS) block calling. main() optionally loads period-6 TRF rows, then for each chromosome (faidx) calls hit_mask (uses _spread) to mark bases covered by perfect or one-mismatch TTAGGG/CCCTAA 6-mers, scans 300-bp windows, merges dense windows into telomere blocks, trims them, scores strand and terminal status, and writes a block table and a per-chromosome summary. one_mismatch_variants runs at import to build VAR_F/VAR_R but those sets are not used by hit_mask. read_fasta and rc are defined but unused by main.
inputs: --genome FASTA (+faidx); --tag; --out; optional --trf 01_trf_calls_extended.tsv; --tel-dist (200000); --min-perfect (0); --max-mismatch (1; 0/1/2); --min-density (0.40); --suffix; env RUN_ID
rule_or_threshold: WIN 300, STEP 150, MIN_DENSITY 0.40, MIN_BLOCK_BP 60, TERMINAL_BP 200000, MAX_MISMATCH 1

what_it_does: Reverse-complements a DNA string. Unused by main.
inputs: sequence

what_it_does: Generator reading a FASTA record by record in upper case. Unused by main (faidx_lite used instead).
inputs: FASTA path

what_it_does: Lists every 6-mer that differs from the telomere motif at no more than one position (the motif itself plus 18 single-base variants). Computed at import into VAR_F and VAR_R, which no other function reads.
inputs: 6-mer motif string
rule_or_threshold: Hamming distance <= 1

what_it_does: Given the start positions of motif hits, marks the 6 bases from each start as covered and returns a per-base True/False mask of chromosome length (difference array + cumulative sum, vectorised).
inputs: numpy array of start positions; sequence length n; k=6
rule_or_threshold: k = 6 bases per hit
